domainTriage.summary: Triaged 53 verified frontend findings down to 47 distinct bugs after merging 6 duplicates. The single release-gate blocker is a CRITICAL auth/security hole: a 2026-06-19 auto-provision trigger grants every open self-signup an immediate GLOBAL editor role on the production vault, re-opening a previously-closed critical data-access + tamper hole (paired with the open-signup hardening gap). Below that sit a cluster of HIGH crash/data-loss bugs: two cycle-unguarded folder-tree recursions that stack-overflow the entire Vault on a corrupt parent_id chain (merged), uncaught uPlot/reduce/empty-array render crashes that white-screen results pages, per-keystroke DB writes that destroy the PM undo stack, a bulk Due-date field that silently wipes scheduling data on an accidental blur, a vehicle-mass KPI that double-counts assembly rollups (2x+ wrong), and a checkout re-click race. The dominant systemic patterns are (1) missing cycle/bounds guards on recursive tree walks, (2) uPlot/array render calls not wrapped against degenerate data, (3) React memo/effect dependency-array omissions causing stale closures and defeated memoization, (4) no remount/reset on study/vault context switch, (5) CSV import/export sanitization gaps (formula injection, thousands-separator, unescaped provenance), and (6) optimistic writes firing without permission/validation/await ordering guards.
patterns: Recursive tree-walks with no cycle/depth guard (folder-paths folderPath/folderNamePath, BrowseScreen count()) stack-overflow on a corrupt parent_id chain; sibling walkers in the same files already use guard++<64 or a visited-Set

uPlot / Array operations invoked on potentially-degenerate data without try-catch or length guard (CycleChart new uPlot+setData, LapPanel reduce-with-no-initial, LapSimScreen deltaT[-1], FftRender log-span div-by-zero, derivative div-by-zero, workspace v5 blob) -> white-screen crashes

React dependency-array / stale-closure bugs: memos and effects omit derived deps (GGDiagram envelope, LinePlot fieldKey, useResizeObserver, useMyCapabilities no refetch, CalendarViewClient seedAnchor) or list unstable inline-array/object identities (FftRender, ChannelReportRender, StripChartRender, TableViewClient) defeating memoization or leaving stale options

No state reset on context switch: ResultsScreen has no remount key on study change, GGDiagram envelope stale on data change, games standings module-cache not cleared on sign-out -> previous study/user state leaks into the new context

CSV import/export discipline gaps: formula-injection (csv-export), thousands-separator mis-parse (importDyno), unescaped provenance comments (lapChannelsCsv), unescaped ilike wildcards (useRecordRefs) -> silent corruption or injection

Optimistic writes fire without guards: per-keystroke persist (TaskDetailSheet title/desc), no permission gate (TaskDetailSheet subsystem auto-null), no range/cross-field validation (MRL, calendar start/due ordering, bulk Due wipe), no await-ordering (CreateTaskDialog FK race) -> rejected writes, data loss, confusing toasts

Shared single-hook-instance / shared-error reuse in loops (BrowseScreen multi-delete clobbers earlier errors, BulkActionBar miscounts) and dedup/idempotency gaps (notification dedup id, games retry duplicate insert) -> misleading counts and duplicate rows
Display/UX resolution gaps: raw UUID instead of name (NotificationFeed), org module mislabeled as logs (presence KNOWN_MODULES), role pill over-reports (useMyRole) -> opaque/misleading UI
Date object mutation via setHours (taskState) and in-place tile mutation (migrateV4ToV5) violate non-mutation contracts -> latent caller-side corruption

bugs.title: Auto-provision trigger grants every open self-signup immediate GLOBAL editor access to the production vault (critical data-access + tamper hole)
bugs.description: The on_auth_user_created trigger unconditionally inserts a GLOBAL editor role (vault_id NULL) for every new auth.users row. With enable_signup=true and enable_confirmations=false, anyone with the public anon key can self-register, log in instantly, and immediately list/download every file in the production vault and upload/modify files in ANY vault (can_edit_in accepts vault_id IS NULL rows for every vault; storage SELECT/INSERT policies are satisfied by any role row). This re-opens exactly the critical hole that migration 20260511000700 was written to close, and the config.toml comment claiming a fresh user has no role row is now false.
bugs.fix: Change the auto-provisioned baseline role from editor to viewer (or a no-access pending role) so fresh accounts cannot upload/modify and an admin must promote. Combine with a before_user_created hook / email-domain allowlist + email confirmation, and update the now-false config.toml comment and storage-RLS assumption.

bugs.title: Open self-signup has no email-domain allowlist, captcha, before_user_created hook, or email confirmation
bugs.description: enable_signup=true and enable_confirmations=false with no captcha, no before_user_created hook, and no email-domain restriction let any party with the public anon key create an immediately-signed-in account with an arbitrary email. Client-side signup does no email-format/domain validation. This is the enabling condition that turns the auto-provision-editor trigger into a full breach and is a standalone hardening gap (spam accounts, self-selected officer-subteam metadata surfaced in the admin panel).
bugs.fix: Add a before_user_created auth hook or email-domain allowlist (e.g. @asu.edu), enable a captcha provider, consider admin approval, and add client-side email format/domain validation in CredentialsStep. Defense-in-depth even after the trigger role default is fixed.

bugs.title: folderPath / folderNamePath / BrowseScreen count() recurse with no cycle guard — corrupt parent_id chain stack-overflows the entire Vault
bugs.description: Three recursive folder-tree walkers traverse parent_id with NO cycle/depth guard. folderPath()/folderNamePath() (folder-paths.ts:51-58,78-84) recurse forever on a cyclic or self-parent chain, throwing RangeError; folderPath is on hot paths (vaultRelativePath/matchLocal, every sync match) so the whole Vault UI becomes unopenable. BrowseScreen fileCountByFolder count() (679-686) memoizes only AFTER recursing, so a cycle recurses infinitely and crashes the Browse tab. Sibling walkers in the SAME files (isDescendantOf/nearestLiveAncestor/resolveBreadcrumbPath with guard++<64; selectedFiles useMemo with an explicit stack/Set) already degrade gracefully. Migration 20260619000200 proves cyclic chains are an anticipated case.
bugs.fix: Rewrite all three as iterative walks with a guard++<64 cap and/or a visited-id Set, returning the partial path / a sentinel on overflow; for count() write total.set(id,0) before recursing or add a visiting Set returning 0 on re-entry. Mirror the existing guarded siblings.
bugs.rank_note: merged BrowseScreen count() cycle-crash into the folder-paths cycle-crash: same root cause (unguarded parent_id recursion / corrupt chain) and identical fix

bugs.title: Bulk 'Due' date field clears due dates on ALL selected tasks when blurred while empty
bugs.description: The bulk-edit Due input is uncontrolled (starts empty) and onBlur unconditionally calls commitDue(e.currentTarget.value); commitDue('') maps to apply({due_date:null}) -> bulkUpdateTasks over every selected id. There is no guard that the user entered/changed a date, so merely focusing and tabbing/clicking away fires a blur with '' and wipes the due_date of every selected task. On a large multi-select this silently erases scheduling data the team depends on for Gantt/calendar/deadlines.
bugs.fix: Only commit when the value is non-empty or when it actually changed from the field's initial value; require an explicit 'Clear due date' action for the null case rather than treating an empty blur as a clear.

bugs.title: TaskDetailSheet title/description inputs fire updateTask + a DB write on every keystroke, destroying the undo stack
bugs.description: The title input (line 294) and description textarea (line 477) call updateTask(task.id, {title/description}) in onChange. updateTask synchronously calls persist() -> db.patchTask() per keystroke plus a server-side activity-row trigger, and pushes one undo entry per character (UNDO_CAP=100). A 20-char edit consumes 20% of the undo budget, making multi-field undo impossible after ~100 keystrokes; the activity feed is one row per character; every keystroke is a DB round-trip.
bugs.fix: Use local controlled state for title/description and call updateTask only on onBlur or Enter, or at minimum debounce the persist by ~400ms.

bugs.title: Vehicle mass total double-counts assembly rollup mass against its own parts (KPI 2x+ inflated)
bugs.description: aggregateMass() adds extractMassGrams(file._properties) into totalGrams and the per-subsystem map for EVERY FileMassRow with no leaf/assembly distinction. SolidWorks stores a computed rollup Mass on assembly (.SLDASM) versions equal to the sum of children, so every leaf gram is recounted for each ancestor assembly carrying a Mass property; nesting compounds at each level (2x or more). The sibling flattenBom deliberately guards this (effectiveMass = isAssembly ? null : node.massGrams) — aggregateMass has no equivalent, so the headline Vehicle Mass KPI and weight-budget over/under-target delta are inflated.
bugs.fix: Exclude assembly rollup mass from totalGrams and bySubsystem (skip names ending .SLDASM / type=assembly, or pass the BOM graph and only sum leaf parts) the same way bom.ts does. Keep assemblies in the heaviest[] ranking for display if desired.

bugs.title: CycleChart: new uPlot(...) and setData() not wrapped in try-catch — degenerate data white-screens the results page
bugs.description: CycleChart calls new uPlot(opts,data,host) (line 109) and plotRef.current.setData(data) (line 126) with no try-catch, while the sibling LinePlot wraps both equivalents (lines 225-234, 249-253). uPlot throws on degenerate data shapes; because both calls are inside layout/data effects, an unhandled exception propagates and unmounts the results page. If cycles is transiently empty or has mismatched series count during study loading, the Single-RPM / Sweep results page crashes with a white screen.
bugs.fix: Wrap the new uPlot(...) call in try-catch (setting plotRef.current=null on failure so the setData effect short-circuits) and wrap setData() in try-catch, mirroring LinePlot.

bugs.title: LapPanelRender LegacyStaticTable crashes on empty laps (reduce with no initial value)
bugs.description: LegacyStaticTable calls laps.reduce((a,b)=>b.time_ms<a.time_ms?b:a).time_ms (line 146) with no initial accumulator. An empty laps array throws TypeError 'Reduce of empty array with no initial value', producing an unhandled React white-screen for any workspace with a legacy static lap config whose laps array is empty. The line-44 length guard is a single render-time read that a race / corrupt config / direct laps=[] can bypass.
bugs.fix: Guard before the reduce: if (laps.length===0) return a 'no laps' node; or supply a safe initial value laps.reduce((a,b)=>...,laps[0]!) after a length check.

bugs.title: SteeringWheelRender cursor subscription calls draw() directly instead of drawRef.current() — stale closure on config/slice change
bugs.description: The cursor subscription (lines 38-42) calls the inline draw() from the render closure rather than through a ref. Unlike RoundGauge/BarGauge/EngineBar (which use drawRef.current=draw), SteeringWheel has no drawRef, so during config/slice changes there is a window where cursor scrub events invoke the stale draw closure with the old channelId/maxAngle/invert, briefly showing incorrect data.
bugs.fix: Add const drawRef = useRef(()=>{}); drawRef.current = draw; and call drawRef.current() in the subscription, matching RoundGaugeRender.

bugs.title: CheckOutButton re-click guard resets in finally before confirm dialog closes — allows concurrent checkout / duplicate lock RPC
bugs.description: handleClick's finally (lines 158-161) unconditionally sets checkingRef.current=false and setChecking(false). When a where-used warning is detected the try calls setWhereUsedConfirm and returns at line 153, but finally still runs — so the button re-enables while the confirm dialog is open. A second click can re-enter handleClick, fetch where-used again, and if the second fetch finds no warning call doCheckOut() while the first dialog is still open; confirming the first dialog then fires doCheckOut() again -> two concurrent acquireLock.run(fileId) calls / duplicate lock RPC.
bugs.fix: Do not reset checkingRef in finally when the early return is due to a where-used warning; track a confirmPending flag and reset checkingRef/checking only after the dialog resolves (both onConfirm and onClose).

bugs.title: CreateTaskDialog races task INSERT against dependency / extra-subteam inserts (FK violation, silent data loss)
bugs.description: onSubmit calls onCreate(task) (addTask) then immediately fires addTaskSubteam and addDependency, each issuing its own fire-and-forget persist() (persist = void run(client)). With no await/serialization, insertTaskSubteam/insertDependency can reach Postgres before insertTask commits, violating the task_subteams.task_id / task_dependencies.*_id FK. The task persists but the extra membership/dependency is rejected and rolled back after showing optimistically, so it silently vanishes on the next refresh plus a confusing FK toast humanized as 'refers to something that no longer exists.' addTask already persists extras in an ordered chain when passed via the task object.
bugs.fix: Pass extraSubteamIds + dependency lists into addTask so a single persist() runs insertTask first then the dependent inserts sequentially, or have addTask return an awaitable the dialog awaits before calling addTaskSubteam/addDependency.

bugs.title: GGDiagram: longitudinal axis (maxLong) floored against muLat instead of muLong — Y scale wrong whenever muLat != muLong
bugs.description: Line 51 uses muLat*1.2 as the floor for the longitudinal (Y) axis extent instead of muLong*1.2 (line 50 correctly uses muLat for the lateral axis). In typical FSAE configs muLat>muLong, so the Y axis is made artificially tall, compressing longitudinal data and distorting the friction ellipse relative to the grid; braking/acceleration limits appear visually compressed, misleading performance-margin reads.
bugs.fix: Change line 51 to const maxLong = Math.max(muLong*1.2, ...longG.map(Math.abs).filter(Number.isFinite))*1.06;

bugs.title: GGDiagram: envelope useMemo uses stale pixel-coordinate closure when only latG/longG data changes
bugs.description: The envelope useMemo (60-70) calls px(lat)/py(lon) which close over maxLat/maxLong/cx/sx/sy, but its dep array is only [muLat,muLong,width,height]. When latG/longG change (switching study, or autocross<->endurance in LapSimScreen), maxLat/maxLong recompute (changing sx/sy) but the memo does not rerun, so the friction ellipse is drawn at stale pixel coordinates — too small/large/misaligned vs the new scatter scale.
bugs.fix: Add maxLat and maxLong (or sx/sy/cx) to the useMemo deps, or move the ellipse computation out of the memo into the render body.

bugs.title: Result screens keep stale local UI state when the active study changes (no remount key)
bugs.description: ResultsScreen renders SingleRpm/Sweep/Optimization results with study={activeStudy} and no key; setActiveStudy swaps only activeStudyId, so switching between two studies of the same kind reconciles the same instance and all useState persists: SweepResults dynoError/dynoWarn/expandedRpm/waveViewerRpm, OptimizationResults selectedIdx/sweepSeedTrial/paramForScatter/sortKey/etc. paramForScatter seeded once from study.parameterPaths[0] makes the scatter filter drop every trial when study B lacks that path, rendering an empty chart with a stale axis label and leftover dyno banners from the previous study.
bugs.fix: Give each rendered results component key={activeStudy.id} to force a clean remount + state reset on every study switch.

bugs.title: Dyno CSV import mis-parses thousands-grouped integers as decimal commas (~1000x silent corruption)
bugs.description: parseNum() treats any cell matching /^-?\d+,\d+$/ as a European decimal comma and does replace(',','.'). That regex also matches a US thousands-grouped integer like '10,000', and the delimiter is chosen as whichever splits the header into the most columns, so in a tab/semicolon-delimited dyno export the comma is NOT the field delimiter and '10,000' survives as one cell -> Number('10.000')=10. rpm/power/torque are silently corrupted ~1000x and the dyno overlay + RMSE/bias vs sim are computed against garbage with no error surfaced.
bugs.fix: Disambiguate before converting: treat one comma followed by exactly three digits and no dot as a thousands group (strip it); only treat the comma as a decimal when the fractional group length is not 3, or detect locale once from all cells.

bugs.title: Notification dedup id embeds receive-time timestamp, so re-delivered events are not de-duplicated
bugs.description: makeId() builds the id as `${table}:${eventType}:${rowId}:${at}` and its doc claims deterministic replay dedup, but `at` is stamped at receive time (new Date().toISOString() in useNotifications.ts:109), not derived from the event row. mergeNotifications dedups solely by id. On a websocket reconnect/resubscribe the same postgres_changes event gets a different wall-clock `at`, hence a different id, and is treated as a brand-new notification — duplicate items and an inflated unread count. Unit tests pass a fixed AT, masking it.
bugs.fix: Derive the dedup component of the id from stable event-row data (version row id, lock id, or created_at/released_at/deleted_at from newRow); keep `at` only as the display timestamp, not part of the id.

bugs.title: Property-aware search makes filename matching case-sensitive when prop: tokens are present
bugs.description: scoreText = hasPropFilters ? parsed.text : rawQ.toLowerCase() (line 76). parsed.text preserves original case (propertySearch.ts:82 pushes m[5] un-lowercased), while score() lowercases only the filename and compares via n.indexOf(q)/ch===q[i]. So with any prop: token a mixed-case free-text term can never match the lowercased filename, and propertyTextMatch only checks property VALUES not filenames. A documented combined query like 'bracket prop:Material=steel' silently under-returns whenever the filename term is capitalized.
bugs.fix: Lowercase the free-text needle before scoring: const scoreText = (hasPropFilters ? parsed.text : rawQ).toLowerCase(); (or lowercase q at the top of score()).

bugs.title: BulkActionBar bulkCancel increments fail for restore failures even though the lock was released — success count undercounts
bugs.description: After releaseLock.run(id) succeeds (line 319), a failed local restore (329-331) does fail++; continue without ever reaching ok++. The status 'Cancelled ok/N (fail failed)' then misreports files whose vault-side lock WAS released as failures. A user seeing '0/3 (3 failed)' when all locks were released retries, producing redundant release RPCs that error ('no active lock') and confuse further.
bugs.fix: Increment ok immediately after releaseLock.run(id) succeeds and track local-restore failures separately (restoreFailed++); include both counts in the status string.

bugs.title: BrowseScreen multi-file context-menu delete uses one shared hook instance in a loop — last error clobbers earlier ones
bugs.description: The onConfirm handler loops over targetFiles calling deleteFile.run(f.id) on one shared deleteFile hook whose single .error is overwritten each call. The status message (line 1250) appends deleteFile.error.message, reflecting only the LAST failed RPC. If files 1 and 3 fail but 2 succeeds, file 1's error is silently dropped; the count is correct but the error text is misleading and hinders diagnosis.
bugs.fix: Collect per-file errors in a local array during the loop and display all of them, or report only the count rather than relying on the shared hook's .error for the message.

bugs.title: TaskDetailSheet auto-nulls subsystem via updateTask even when the user has no edit permission
bugs.description: The effect clearing a now-invalid subsystem (232-237) runs for any opened task regardless of canEdit/editPerm.allowed, although canEdit gates every other interactive field. teamSubsystems is derived from localStorage recallSharing plus subsystems; if the sharing map isn't loaded or a valid shared subsystem isn't in this browser's localStorage, the check is false for a legitimately-valid subsystem, so a viewer/non-owner triggers an optimistic updateTask that RLS rejects and rolls back — a spurious 'Change not saved' toast just from viewing, repeatable on every refresh.
bugs.fix: Gate the auto-clear effect on canEdit so only owners/leads/admins issue the corrective write, and ideally only fire it on an in-session primary-subteam change rather than on every render/refresh.

bugs.title: MRL input allows out-of-range values (0, negative, >9) without client-side rejection
bugs.description: The MRL input (376-378) converts the raw string directly to a number with no range check before updateTask. HTML min/max prevent the stepper but not manual keyboard entry; the DB CHECK (mrl 1-9) rejects the write, rolls back, and snaps the field, but no inline error is shown — the only feedback is the subtle global WriteErrorToast.
bugs.fix: Add a client-side range check before updateTask (accept empty or integer 1..9) and show an inline validation message when out of range.

bugs.title: Calendar drag-to-reschedule does not validate date ordering (start_date can be set after due_date)
bugs.description: handleDragEnd (line 414) unconditionally calls updateTask with the new start_date or due_date with no check that start<=due; the date inputs in TaskDetailSheet (432-452) share the omission. A user can drag a start chip past the due date, creating a logically invalid task (start>due); the Gantt's Math.max(1,...) masks it as a 1-day bar, but scheduling / critical-path calcs assuming start<=due produce wrong results.
bugs.fix: In handleDragEnd, after resolving the date, assert start<=due (kind start) / due>=start (kind due) against the existing opposite date; refuse or toast on violation. Apply the same guard to the TaskDetailSheet date inputs.

bugs.title: Module-level leaderboard cache never cleared on user sign-out (cross-user data exposure)
bugs.description: cache/inflight/listeners/cacheClient are module-level globals living for the renderer process lifetime; the only eviction compares cacheClient reference identity (58-63). If the Supabase client object is reused/pooled after sign-out/sign-in, user B's standings view shows user A's cached leaderboard (display names, scores) until a background fetch completes. Read-only standings, not credentials, but still cross-user data exposure on a shared machine.
bugs.fix: Hook the auth shell's user-change/sign-out event to call cache.clear()+notify(), or key cache entries on user_id so each user's data is isolated.

bugs.title: Leaderboard individual player ranks ignore ties — consecutive ranks/medals assigned
bugs.description: toEntries() assigns rank: i+1 unconditionally by sorted index, so two players with identical best scores get ranks 1 and 2 (and gold vs silver medal chips) instead of sharing rank 1. The subteams path already does competition ranking via subteamRanks() (standings.tsx:147-155); the per-player path does not.
bugs.fix: Implement standard competition ranking in toEntries: track the previous row's best and only advance the rank counter when it changes, mirroring subteamRanks().

bugs.title: Malformed sweep import (missing lastCycle) crashes torque-curve / summary / fuel-map readers
bugs.description: studyFromBundle()'s sweep branch defensively guards only the cycles array, not lastCycle (a required CycleStats field on SweepPoint). Downstream sweep consumers dereference p.lastCycle.<field> with no guard (torqueCurveFromSweep maps p.lastCycle.brakeTorqueNm before its finite filter; peakOf/summarizeSweep/powerbandWidth read brakePowerKW/brakeTorqueNm/veAtm/knockIntegral; fuelMapFromSweep reads indicatedPowerKW/brakePowerKW/intakeMassPerCycleG). A hand-edited/corrupt bundle omitting lastCycle yields lastCycle===undefined, so importing it and opening the sweep on the Performance/Sweep screen throws and crashes the CFD render instead of the intended per-study skip-with-warning.
bugs.fix: In the sweep branch, drop or reject points lacking a usable lastCycle (filter on isObj(p.lastCycle) or throw a per-study 'corrupt sweep point' warning so the bundle is skipped, matching the existing skip-with-warning contract), and/or make the downstream readers null-safe on lastCycle.

bugs.title: 'org' module missing from KNOWN_MODULES — Org users always shown as 'Logs' in presence roster
bugs.description: KNOWN_MODULES lists only logs/vault/cfd/pm/games, but ModuleId includes 'org' and the picker renders an 'org' nav button. track() sends module:'org', and any peer's asModule('org') falls through to the 'logs' default, so every Org session is mislabeled as Logs in the presence roster.
bugs.fix: Add 'org' to the KNOWN_MODULES set.

bugs.title: Drag-dropped .helios workspace bundles are silently dropped (advertised drag-import is dead)
bugs.description: useFileDrop filters out every dropped .helios path on the assumption they are routed through useFileOpener, but useFileOpener only listens to the Rust helios://open-files event + get_pending_open_files drain (OS launch / file-association), never webview drag-drop. App.tsx wires useFileDrop to data files only, so a .helios bundle dragged onto the window is discarded with no import dialog and no error — while load-user-session.ts:85 actively advertises a drag-to-import gesture that does nothing.
bugs.fix: In useFileDrop, split out .helios paths and forward them to a bundle-import callback (readTextFile+parseBundle+onPending) or route them into the same handler useFileOpener.onPending feeds; otherwise remove the misleading 'drag to import' copy.

bugs.title: CSV export is vulnerable to spreadsheet formula injection via channel ids/units
bugs.description: csvCell() quotes only cells containing [",\n] and does not neutralize formula-injection prefixes (=,+,-,@,tab,CR). The export header/units rows come from channel ids/units; for an unknown CSV column the Rust registry synthesizes id/display_name verbatim from the raw header text. So a malicious CSV header like =HYPERLINK(...)/@SUM(...)/=cmd|'/c calc'!A1 becomes a channel id written verbatim into row 1 of the Helios-generated export; a teammate who loads it, exports, and opens the result in Excel/Sheets can trigger attacker-controlled formula evaluation (HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE exfiltration, DDE). The export looks trustworthy because Helios generated it.
bugs.fix: In csvCell, prefix any cell whose first char is =,+,-,@,\t,\r with a leading apostrophe before quoting; apply to all cells including header and units rows.

bugs.title: useResizeObserver: stale onResize in deps causes observer reconnect on every render
bugs.description: The effect deps are [ref, onResize] (line 28). Any caller passing a non-stable inline callback tears down and re-creates the ResizeObserver on every parent render, risking missed resize events during rapid re-renders and a ResizeObserver loop if an unstable callback causes a state update on each fire.
bugs.fix: Capture onResize in an internal ref (onResizeRef.current=onResize) and call onResizeRef.current(...) inside a single stable observer callback; remove onResize from deps so the observer is recreated only when the element ref changes.

bugs.title: taskOutlineState / daysUntilDue mutate the caller's Date object via setHours()
bugs.description: Both taskOutlineState (line 33) and daysUntilDue (line 69) call today.setHours(0,0,0,0) on the passed-in Date, which mutates the object in-place. Any caller reusing that Date across calls sees it silently modified, causing off-by-one-day bugs or wrong display times (e.g. toLocaleDateString showing midnight).
bugs.fix: Replace today.setHours(0,0,0,0) with a non-mutating new Date(today.getFullYear(),today.getMonth(),today.getDate()).getTime() and use that value in the arithmetic.

bugs.title: FftRender: log-scale x-to-canvas division by zero when fMax === fMinPlot — trace silently disappears
bugs.description: In log freqScale, xToCanvas divides by (log10(fMax)-log10(fMinPlot)). When fMax===fMinPlot (single-bin spectrum, or fmaxHz clamped to fMinPlot) the denominator is 0 -> Infinity for every x; Canvas silently ignores Infinity coords so the whole trace disappears with no error. The line-107 guard only catches fMax<=0.
bugs.fix: Compute logSpan once, use safeLogSpan = logSpan>0 ? logSpan : 1, and add an early-out 'not enough frequency range' when fMax<=fMinPlot.

bugs.title: ZoneStatsRender: every 60Hz cursor tick triggers a full React re-render + per-channel aggregateZone
bugs.description: The cursor subscription (line 64) calls setCursorUs(t) on every tick, scheduling a full re-render of ZoneStatsRender plus all useMemo/aggregateZone work. At 60Hz pointer drag this is 60 full renders/sec including per-channel aggregation, dropping effective frame rate on large sessions.
bugs.fix: Use a ref for cursorUs and only setState when the zone boundary actually changes, or throttle to requestAnimationFrame cadence using the raf-gating pattern from TireGridRender.

bugs.title: StripChartRender: speedByOverlay useMemo lists unstable slice object in deps, defeating the memo
bugs.description: The speedByOverlay useMemo deps (line 295) include slice, which is typically a new object reference on every parent render (store subscriptions). So it recomputes every render — including distance mode where perSampleLapDistance runs per session — even though session identity is already captured by the visibleIdsKey dep.
bugs.fix: Remove slice from the speedByOverlay deps; if speed data must refresh on data changes, signal that via a session version stamp rather than object identity.

bugs.title: FftRender: spectra useMemo depends on inline-built visible array identity, defeating O(n log n) FFT memoization
bugs.description: The spectra useMemo deps list visible (line 57), which is built inline as a new array every render (lines 26-28). magnitudeSpectrum (O(n log n)) thus recomputes on every parent render including cursor moves and config-panel interactions, causing frame drops on large datasets (100k+ samples).
bugs.fix: Stabilize with const visibleIdsKey = JSON.stringify(visible.map(v=>v.id)) and use [visibleIdsKey, config, viewState] as deps, matching StripChartRender.

bugs.title: Background refresh/hydrate unconditionally clears lastWriteError, suppressing the 'Change not saved' toast
bugs.description: hydrate() always sets lastWriteError:null and runs on every background refresh path. The refresh() guard only aborts when inFlightWrites>0 or writeEpoch changed DURING the fetch — it does not protect against clearing an error from a write that already completed. A failed write (sets lastWriteError, inFlightWrites drains to 0) followed by any background refresh landing within the 6s toast window nulls lastWriteError before the user sees it, so a rolled-back change is never surfaced.
bugs.fix: Do not unconditionally clear lastWriteError in hydrate during background refreshes; clear it only on initial hydrate, explicit user dismiss, or the next successful user write.

bugs.title: useMyCapabilities never refetches — self-/newly-granted permissions stay stale (gated controls disabled) until full app reload
bugs.description: useMyCapabilities loads caps in an effect keyed only on client and returns no refetch. All three Org panels gate admin controls on its can(); after a grant/revoke only usePeople().refetch() runs, so the local can() never refreshes. An owner/exec who just received or self-granted a capability still sees Structure/Role-Editor/People controls disabled until the whole app reloads, and may conclude the grant failed. Server re-checks every write (fail-closed), so no security impact.
bugs.fix: Expose a refetch() from useMyCapabilities (mirroring the other hooks' tick pattern) and call it after successful grant/revoke/role-edit mutations, or subscribe to an org-mutation event.

bugs.title: Role Editor sends disabled-but-checked capabilities — a partial-cap manage-roles admin cannot edit (even rename) any role containing a cap they lack
bugs.description: In RoleCard each capability checkbox is checked={selected.has(c.key)} but disabled={...||!can(c.key)}; selected is seeded from role.capabilities, so a cap the editor does NOT hold is shown disabled-yet-checked and stays in selected. save() always sends [...selected] to pm.upsert_role, whose server edit-subset guard requires the array be a subset of the caller's caps else it raises 'cannot define a role with capabilities you do not hold', rejecting the ENTIRE upsert. So a custom role granting org.manage_roles plus only a subset of caps lets a user manage roles yet be unable to edit (even rename/recolor) any role containing a cap they lack — opaque workflow dead-end (server correctly fail-closed).
bugs.fix: Lock the whole RoleCard with an explanatory tooltip when the role contains any cap the caller lacks, or send only caller-holdable + pre-existing accepted caps, or surface a clear pre-save message instead of letting the opaque server rejection surface.

bugs.title: Grant dropdown offers subteam roles a subteam-only granter cannot actually grant (no client-side grant-subset filtering)
bugs.description: For a non-org granter, grantableRoles = roles.filter(r=>r.scope==='subteam') — ALL subteam-scoped roles regardless of whether the caller holds those roles' caps at the chosen subteam. The server's grant_role enforces grant-subset and raises 'cannot grant a role with capabilities you do not hold'. With seeded roles a Lead holds a superset so no error fires, but a custom subteam role granting a cap the Lead lacks (e.g. vault.admin) would appear and produce a server rejection on Add. Latent until such a custom role exists.
bugs.fix: Filter grantableRoles by grant-subset on the client using useRolesWithCaps + useMyCapabilities: only offer subteam roles whose cap set is a subset of the caller's effective caps for the chosen subteam; recompute when the target subteam changes.

bugs.title: useAutoAddDrafts can stall busy-skipped/cancelled candidates until an unrelated external trigger re-fires the effect
bugs.description: The effect early-returns when busyRef is true; if deps change mid-flight the new run is dropped and the old run's cleanup sets cancelled=true (breaking the loop). The finally clears busyRef but never bumps tick to re-arm; the only self-retrigger (deferredFresh setTick) is unreachable on the busy path. So candidates deferred because a run was busy or cut off mid-loop aren't retried until unmatched/tick changes from an unrelated source (a fresh scan or STABLE_AGE timer). Added latency only, no data loss.
bugs.fix: In the finally, when a run ended with work left undone (cancelled mid-loop or skipped because busy), bump an internal tick to re-arm the effect, mirroring the deferredFresh setTick path.

bugs.title: Unresolved-reference warning uses ilike with raw basename — _/% in filenames act as SQL wildcards, producing false 'ambiguous' warnings
bugs.description: Line 57 counts vault files via .ilike('name', base) commented '// no wildcards', but in ILIKE _ matches any single char and % any run. base comes verbatim from child_path_hint and is not escaped; CAD/part filenames commonly contain underscores (Bracket_01.SLDPRT), so the pattern over-matches (BracketX01.SLDPRT), inflating count and flipping reason from 'missing' to 'ambiguous'. Files merely containing an underscore can show the misleading 'rename one to disambiguate' warning — warning-accuracy only, but erodes trust in the cross-reference health surface.
bugs.fix: Escape LIKE metacharacters (%, _, \) in base before the ilike, or replace with a case-insensitive exact match (fetch names and compare lowercased). Fix the misleading comment.

bugs.title: NotificationFeed: actor rendered as raw UUID prefix instead of display name
bugs.description: Line 191 renders 'by {n.actorId.slice(0,8)}…' — an 8-char hex prefix of the actor's UUID — for every item with an actorId. The component receives no user-name map and has no resolution mechanism, unlike WhoHasWhatScreen's resolveHolderName + userById map. Users see opaque strings like 'by a3f912b0…' instead of a teammate's name.
bugs.fix: Pass a userMap: Map<string,string> prop (from useVaultUsers/usePeople at the call site) into NotificationFeed and resolve n.actorId through it, falling back to the short id only when absent.

bugs.title: Team-scoped onCreate re-homes the primary subteam but leaves the dialog-selected subteam as a stray secondary membership
bugs.description: When a view is scoped to a subteam, onCreate builds teamPatched with subteam_id=currentTeam.id but does NOT overwrite task.subteams, which the dialog set to [the dialog-selected subteam]. addTask computes extras = seeded.subteams.filter(s=>s.id!==seeded.subteam_id) and persists the original entry as a secondary membership. So creating a task from a team-scoped board/table/gantt/graph while picking a DIFFERENT subteam in the dialog tags it to BOTH teams instead of re-homing it. Identical pattern in all four view clients.
bugs.fix: When re-homing, also reset subteams to [currentTeam], e.g. {...task, subteam_id: currentTeam.id, subteam: currentTeam, subteams: [currentTeam], subsystem_id: null, subsystem: null}.
bugs.rank_note: merged the TableView/GanttView/GraphView occurrences into the BoardView entry: identical re-home omission and identical fix across all four view clients

bugs.title: Retry submit can insert duplicate score rows on flaky network
bugs.description: onRetrySubmit calls handleGameOver(over.score) again -> submitScore plain INSERT. If the original request reached the DB but the response was lost, the retry inserts a second identical row. Current MAX-aggregation leaderboards are unaffected, but duplicate raw rows accumulate silently in games.scores and will skew any future count/total/average analytics.
bugs.fix: Generate a client UUID before the first submit and pass it as client_id with a UNIQUE constraint so duplicate inserts are rejected, or use ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET score=GREATEST(excluded.score, scores.score).

bugs.title: GameOverOverlay score count-up flashes final value then jumps to 0
bugs.description: useCountUp initializes useState(target) (line 15) so the first render paints the final score, then the useEffect calls setValue(0) (line 25) before animating, producing a visible final-score -> 0 -> count-up flash on every game-over.
bugs.fix: Change useState(target) to useState(0) on line 15; the initial render then shows 0 and the effect animates 0->target with no flash. The reduced-motion path is unaffected.

bugs.title: buildSweepCyclesCsv / buildOptimizationCurvesCsv rebuilt twice per export-menu construction
bugs.description: sweepActions() calls buildSweepCyclesCsv(study) once to decide whether to push the action and again in run() to produce the CSV (same for buildOptimizationCurvesCsv). The presence-check materializes the full CSV string eagerly every time the menu is built, and SweepResults memoizes the menu on [study, summary], so it recomputes on every study object change — each appended point during a live run — doing redundant O(rows) string building.
bugs.fix: Build the CSV once and branch on null: const cyclesCsv = buildSweepCyclesCsv(study); if (cyclesCsv != null) actions.push({..., run: () => saveTextFile(..., cyclesCsv)}); same for the curves CSV.

bugs.title: LapPanelRender: lap row key uses filtered idxInList instead of stable allIdx — DOM node reuse on filter toggle
bugs.description: Lap rows use key=`${session.id}-${idxInList}` where idxInList is the index in the filtered (post hideUntrusted) array. Toggling hideUntrusted shifts positions so React reuses lap N's DOM node for lap M's data, briefly showing stale/highlighted state. The stable allIdx (index in the unfiltered array) is computed one line above but unused as the key.
bugs.fix: Change the key to `${session.id}-${allIdx}` using the already-computed allIdx.

bugs.title: ChannelReportRender: useMemo depends on inline-built visible array identity, defeating per-lap aggregation memo
bugs.description: visible is assigned inline (line 92) as a new array every render, and the useMemo deps (line 113) list visible, so aggregateForLap runs on every parent re-render (cursor moves, config interactions, other widget updates) rather than only on session-data change — non-trivial CPU for many-lap/many-channel sessions.
bugs.fix: Stabilize the dep with const visibleIdsKey = JSON.stringify(visible.map(v=>v.id)) and use visibleIdsKey in the deps, as StripChartRender already does.

bugs.title: LapSimScreen: deltaT[deltaT.length-1]!.toFixed(2) crashes if deltaT is an empty array
bugs.description: The render guard {runB && deltaT && (...)} treats an empty array as truthy; inside, deltaT[deltaT.length-1]!.toFixed(2) reads deltaT[-1]===undefined and throws a TypeError. A lap sim producing zero distance steps (degenerate track) crashes LapSimScreen with a white screen when selecting a B lap in compare mode.
bugs.fix: Use deltaT.length>0 ? deltaT[deltaT.length-1]!.toFixed(2) : '0.00', or add deltaT.length>0 && to the outer render condition.

bugs.title: LinePlot: fieldKey omits series[i].showPoints and series[i].width — structural plot options silently stale after prop change
bugs.description: fieldKey (96-98) encodes only label/color/axis/xs-present, omitting showPoints and width which are structural uPlot options set only at construction. If a parent changes only showPoints or width, fieldKey is unchanged, the layout effect does not rebuild, and the stale structural options remain (setData updates data arrays only). Currently latent because showPoints is always false and not toggled, but will silently activate if dynamic toggling is added.
bugs.fix: Append :${s.width ?? ''}:${s.showPoints ?? ''} to each series segment in the fieldKey map.

bugs.title: Lap-channel CSV provenance comments interpolate config/vehicle/track names without escaping
bugs.description: The '#'-prefixed comment lines embed meta.configName/vehicleName/trackName via template strings (38-40) with no CR/LF stripping or quoting, unlike the numeric data rows. A newline in a name splits the comment preamble into an apparent extra row, and an embedded comma changes the apparent header field structure, confusing downstream Excel/MATLAB/MoTeC importers. Names are user-influenceable (config/vehicle names).
bugs.fix: Strip CR/LF (and ideally collapse commas) from the interpolated names before embedding, mirroring the cell-sanitizing discipline of the rest of the export layer.

bugs.title: derivative() divides by zero on duplicate adjacent timestamps, emitting non-finite spikes
bugs.description: All three difference branches (forward i=0, central interior, backward i=N-1) divide by a time delta with no zero-guard. Equal neighboring sample times (duplicated rows or a low-resolution time column) make the denominator 0 -> ±Infinity (or NaN). The module's contract is to emit NaN for uncomputable samples and the sibling ops (integral/smooth/lowpass/highpass) all guard their inputs — derivative is the outlier. A math channel using derivative over dirty CSV poisons downstream arithmetic and blows out auto-scaled y-axes.
bugs.fix: Guard each delta: const dt = t1-t0; out[i] = dt!==0 ? (v1-v0)/dt : NaN; for all three branches.

bugs.title: loadWorkspaces returns current-version blob without validating per-workspace shape
bugs.description: When version===CURRENT_VERSION (5), loadWorkspaces returns parsed.workspaces after only Array.isArray + length>0, performing none of the per-workspace structural validation parseBundle does (string id/label/color + Array tiles). A corrupted/hand-edited v5 blob (e.g. a workspace missing tiles) parses without a JSON error, bypasses the try/catch, and reaches the renderer where .tiles.map/snapTile throws and can white-screen with no fallback to built-ins. Requires a tampered/corrupt blob.
bugs.fix: Run the same structural validation parseBundle uses over parsed.workspaces in the version===CURRENT_VERSION branch; on failure fall through to the existing seed-builtins recovery.

bugs.title: useMyRole falls back to the most-privileged role across ALL vaults — sidebar role pill can over-report
bugs.description: When a user has no global (vault_id NULL) row, useMyRole resolves the pill to best = the single most-privileged role row across every vault, irrespective of the current vault. A user who is admin in vault X but viewer in vault Y shows 'admin' while working in Y. Display-only — all real authorization is enforced server-side per-vault via is_admin_in/can_edit_in — and the 20260619000700 trigger now gives most users a global row so the fallback rarely fires.
bugs.fix: If the pill is a global indicator, document it; otherwise resolve the role for the active vault id (global row else that vault's per-vault row) rather than the global max across all vaults.

bugs.title: migrateV4ToV5 directly mutates tile objects via a shallow-copied array
bugs.description: Line 147 shallow-copies the tiles array ([...w.tiles]) but the loop (150-153) mutates the original TileSpec objects in place (t.w=0.22, t.x=0.42, etc.), inconsistent with migrateV2ToV3's .map()+spread. Latent today because callers pass JSON.parse'd fresh objects, but a future refactor passing live Workspace state would silently corrupt tile layout in the caller.
bugs.fix: Replace the mutation loop with a .map() returning {...t, w/x:...} for matching tiles and t otherwise.

bugs.title: lapAggregate per-lap accumulation includes the lap-end boundary sample, double-attributing it to adjacent laps
bugs.description: Laps are half-open [startUs,endUs) and contiguous (lap N's endUs == lap N+1's startUs). The accumulation loop uses `if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;`, so a sample at exactly lap.endUs is processed for lap N (no break on equality) AND lap N+1 (its tUs<startUs is false at startUs), contributing to both laps' max/min/mean/last/first and inflating lap_mean's denominator. The broadcast loop below uses the half-open `tUs >= endUs`, so the two halves are inconsistent. Reachable for beacon/expression crossings whose pushed tUs equals a real boundary sample.
bugs.fix: Change `if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;` to `if (tUs >= lap.endUs) break;` so the per-lap loop matches the half-open broadcast semantics.

bugs.title: lapIndexAt returns the last lap index for timestamps before the first lap
bugs.description: After the containing-lap scan fails, the tail fallback `return tUs <= last.endUs ? laps.length-1 : -1;` returns the LAST lap index for ANY tUs<=last.endUs, including tUs strictly before laps[0].startUs (a cursor before the first sample, or a manual-crossing config whose first lap doesn't start at the data origin). The sibling lapAt() also requires tUs>=last.startUs; lapIndexAt is missing that lower bound, so the two disagree at head-of-session and lap-aware widgets mis-attribute those samples to the final lap.
bugs.fix: Mirror lapAt's bounds: return (tUs>=last.startUs && tUs<=last.endUs) ? laps.length-1 : -1;

bugs.title: addChannel replace path leaves a stale source_header binding when re-adding a channel id with a changed/absent source_header
bugs.description: addChannel allows replacing an existing channel id but #bySourceHeader is first-write-wins, and the replace branch never cleans up the id's prior source_header binding. Re-adding the id with a different/absent source_header orphans the old oldHeader->id entry; effectiveChannelId/setChannelOverride resolve through #bySourceHeader, so an override targeting oldHeader still redirects to this id and listSourceHeaders still advertises the stale header. removeChannel implements owner-aware cleanup for exactly this hazard; addChannel does not. Edge case (ingested CSV channels aren't replaced, most math channels have no source_header).
bugs.fix: On the replace path, before re-binding, drop any existing #bySourceHeader entry whose value===meta.id but whose key!==meta.source_header (mirror removeChannel's owner-aware cleanup), then set the new binding.

bugs.title: seedAnchor in CalendarViewClient is computed once with an empty dependency array
bugs.description: seedAnchor is a useMemo reading baseTasks/milestones but declaring [] deps (eslint-disabled), computed once at mount, and is then passed as the initial value to useState (read once). If the component mounts from cache with an empty/stale task list, seedAnchor defaults to today; after the network hydrates tasks with dates weeks/months away the anchor stays at today and the user must navigate manually to find their tasks.
bugs.fix: Add baseTasks/milestones to the memo deps and use a useState lazy initializer with a ref guard that computes the seed only when the first non-empty dataset arrives (useState(()=>computeSeed(baseTasks,milestones))).

bugs.title: TableViewClient renderRow creates new closures every render, preventing row-level bailout
bugs.description: renderRow is a plain function in the component body (not useCallback) called via visibleParents.map((t)=>renderRow(t,0)) and recursively, passing inline arrow callbacks; RowFragment is a plain (non-memo) component. Every prop is a new reference each render, so React cannot bail out any row even when its data is unchanged — any store selector update (e.g. one status change) re-renders every row, producing visible jank with 100+ tasks.
bugs.fix: Wrap RowFragment in React.memo, stabilize per-row callback props with useCallback, or extract a memoized row component that reads its own data via a usePmStore selector so it re-renders only when its task changes.

domainTriage.summary: 14 verified findings triaged to 9 distinct bugs after merging 5 duplicates. The release-gate blockers are two crash/availability defects: an unwrapped single-RPM solver call that permanently wedges all future single-RPM studies on a panic (runner.rs), and a path-traversal in cfd_load_capture letting an XSS'd renderer read files outside the captures root (commands.rs). A second tier of correctness defects all share a single root cause: helios-csv hardcodes a comma delimiter throughout the MoTeC/Link preamble path, causing hard load failures and unit-hint loss for non-US-locale vendor CSVs. The engine-sim config loader and valve table reads are riddled with unchecked indexing/unwrap() on user-controlled JSON that should return ConfigLoadError::Schema. Recurring systemic issues: (1) inconsistent panic-isolation wiring across the three CFD run paths, (2) pervasive index-without-bounds-check on untrusted config JSON, (3) hardcoded comma delimiter assumption in CSV parsing, (4) missing input-field traversal guards that sibling functions already implement.

bugs.title: Single-RPM solver panic is not isolated — worker unwinds, job stuck 'Running' forever, permanently blocking all future single-RPM studies
bugs.description: run_single_rpm_job calls eng.advance_one_cycle(...) bare at runner.rs:340 with NO run_engine_unwind_safe wrapper and NO SilencedPanicHook, unlike the sweep (runner.rs:533) and inline (runner.rs:727) paths which both wrap the identical call. The SDM26 solver panic!s on positivity failure / junction non-convergence; DefaultDivergenceProbe only screens non-finite CycleStats after a cycle completes and never sees a panic. The job runs in a bare std::thread::spawn closure (commands.rs:156) whose terminal status write (commands.rs:198-199) follows the run_* call with no catch_unwind, so an unwinding panic skips it and JobHandle.status stays Running. CfdState::register (state.rs:69-77) rejects any new same-kind job while one is Running, so the user can never start another single-RPM study for the rest of the session. Promoted to critical for the release gate: a single bad config/RPM permanently disables a whole study mode with no error surfaced.
bugs.fix: Mirror the sweep path: install SilencedPanicHook for the cycle loop and wrap the eng.advance_one_cycle call (and capture pass) in run_engine_unwind_safe, converting a caught panic into a JobErrorEvent with ErrorReason::SolverDiverged and returning RunOutcome::Errored as the sweep worker does at runner.rs:540-557. Additionally wrap the run_* dispatch in commands.rs in catch_unwind so the terminal status is always recorded even on an unexpected unwind.

bugs.title: cfd_load_capture interpolates unvalidated job_id into the read path — directory traversal outside the captures root
bugs.description: cfd_load_capture validates `file` against ../slash/backslash (commands.rs:288) and whitelists it plus study_kind, but job_id is joined directly into the read target at commands.rs:305 with no traversal check and no canonicalize/path_under guard. A job_id containing `..` segments escapes <Documents>/Helios/cfd/captures and lets a compromised/XSS'd renderer read any JSON-parseable file whose path tail matches /single-rpm|sweep/<u32>/{pv,profiles,manifest}.json, returning its parsed content to the page. The sibling load_waves_from_dir (crates/cfd-core/src/load.rs:56-58) already rejects ../slash/backslash in job_id and path_under() exists and is already used at commands.rs:55 — proving the guard was known and simply missed here. (Note: cfd_load_waves IS already guarded; only cfd_load_capture is vulnerable.)
bugs.fix: Reject job_id containing `..`, `/`, or `\` (or restrict to the ULID charset, since job ids are ULIDs) exactly as load_waves_from_dir does, then canonicalize the built path and verify path_under(&p, &root) before reading.

bugs.title: Non-comma (semicolon/tab) MoTeC and Link CSV exports fail to load; units/cell parsing also hardcodes comma
bugs.description: Merged 2 findings sharing one root cause: the MoTeC/Link preamble path hardcodes a comma delimiter throughout. strip_motec()/strip_link() rebuild the channel-name header via dedupe_csv_header() using a default-COMMA csv::ReaderBuilder + WriterBuilder (load.rs:303-373); on a semicolon/tab-delimited source the comma reader collapses the whole header into one quoted cell. detect_delimiter() then runs on the rewritten header and selects ';' (the surviving embedded separators), so data rows split into N fields while the header is 1 field -> csv returns Csv(UnequalLengths) and the file fails to load (empirically reproduced: LOAD(semicolon)=Err(UnequalLengths{expected:1,len:3}), LOAD_TAB=Err, LOAD_COMMA=Ok). The SAME hardcoded-comma root cause also breaks parse_units_line()/count_csv_cells() (load.rs:385-406): the units row is read as a single cell, so per-channel unit hints (prepared.units.get(i)) collapse and semantic disambiguation (kPa vs degC) is lost — this is the residual defect once the load failure is fixed. Plain non-preamble CSVs are unaffected (detection runs on the raw first line, no re-serialization).
bugs.fix: Detect the delimiter from the ORIGINAL header/data line in strip_motec/strip_link before any re-serialization, then either re-serialize the deduped header with that same delimiter or carry the detected delimiter in CsvInput so load_csv_bytes reads with it directly. dedupe_csv_header, count_csv_cells, and parse_units_line must all use the source delimiter, not a hardcoded comma — fixing both the load failure and the unit-hint loss in one pass.

bugs.title: Config loader panics on malformed JSON (short Cd-table rows, empty pipe arrays, missing/wrong-typed fields) instead of returning ConfigLoadError::Schema
bugs.description: Merged 2 findings sharing one root cause: the v1 JSON config loader indexes and unwraps user-controlled JSON without validation, so a malformed config file crashes the whole process at load time (and in a sweep/optimization service aborts the entire job rather than rejecting one config). (a) unpack_cd_table (loader.rs:48-54) checks row.as_array() then indexes r[0]/r[1] directly — a short row like [0.05] or [] panics with index-out-of-bounds; called for both intake and exhaust cd_table on every load_v1_json. (b) load_v1_json requires intake_pipes/exhaust_primaries to be arrays but never checks non-empty, then unconditionally indexes runner_lengths[0], primaries[0], etc. (loader.rs:119-129); empty array panics. Same path uses p["length"].as_f64().unwrap(), p["wall_temperature"].as_f64().unwrap(), and data["firing_order"].as_array().unwrap() with per-element .as_i64().unwrap() (loader.rs:90-128) — all panic on missing/wrong-typed fields. The correct pattern already exists in-tree: spark_advance_map loader (loader.rs:264-269) does an r.len() != 2 check, and req_f64/req_u helpers exist at loader.rs:21-32.
bugs.fix: Validate r.len() >= 2 (or use r.get(0)/r.get(1)) in unpack_cd_table and return ConfigLoadError::Schema, mirroring spark_advance_map. Validate intake_pipes/exhaust_primaries are non-empty before indexing [0]. Replace all .as_f64().unwrap()/.as_array().unwrap()/.as_i64().unwrap() on config JSON with the existing req_f64/req_u-style helpers returning ConfigLoadError::Schema.

bugs.title: valve_cd indexes ld_table[0]/cd_table[0] without empty-table guard; loader accepts empty cd_table
bugs.description: valve_cd reads ld_table[0]/cd_table[0] (valve.rs:168-169) and computes last = ld_table.len() - 1 (valve.rs:171); an empty table makes len()-1 underflow to usize::MAX and the [0] index panics. unpack_cd_table (loader.rs:42-56) produces empty Vecs for an empty `cd_table: []` array without rejecting it; those flow through cfg.intake/exhaust_cd_table -> ValveParams.cd_table (sdm26.rs:848-863) -> valve_cd with no intervening guard, panicking on the first valve-open step. Closely related to the loader-panic cluster (same loader, same empty-input class) but kept separate because the panic site is in the solver, not the loader, and confidence is medium. Severity low: default config and all parity fixtures have non-empty tables; only an explicitly malformed config hits it.
bugs.fix: Reject empty Cd/L-D tables in the loader (require the array non-empty in unpack_cd_table) and/or guard valve_cd to return 0.0 when ld_table.is_empty(). Fix alongside the loader-panic cluster (rank 4).

bugs.title: Process-global panic-hook save/restore races between concurrent CFD jobs of different kinds, can leave a permanent no-op hook
bugs.description: SilencedPanicHook::install (runner.rs:105-109) does process-global take_hook()+set_hook(noop) and Drop restores the saved hook — correct only under strict LIFO nesting. CfdState::register (state.rs:69-77) only rejects a new job whose kind matches a Running job, so different kinds (sweep at runner.rs:501, optimization at runner.rs:985, plus :1219) run concurrently and each touches the global hook. Non-LIFO interleaving (Sweep installs saving REAL hook -> Optimization installs saving the NOOP hook -> Sweep drops restoring REAL -> Optimization drops restoring NOOP) leaves a permanent no-op panic hook, so every subsequent panic in the process prints nothing — badly degrading crash diagnosability for the rest of the session. The doc comment's 'avoids racing set_hook/take_hook across workers' claim is true only intra-job and gives false confidence.
bugs.fix: Do not use the process-global hook for per-region silencing when concurrent jobs are possible. Either (a) serialize all CFD jobs through a global mutex, (b) install a process-lifetime filtering hook once at startup gated by a thread-local 'in solver region' flag, or (c) reference-count installs under a global mutex so the real hook is saved once and restored only when the last region exits.

bugs.title: Sweep worker silently drops an RPM (no point, no error) when zero cycles complete
bugs.description: In the sweep worker, if the per-RPM cycle loop produces no CycleStats (n_cycles_max == 0 so for cycle_i in 0..0 never runs, or the first advance_one_cycle returns TargetReached/Cancelled before any stats are pushed), last_cs = accumulated.last().copied() (runner.rs:600) is None and the if let Some(last) block at runner.rs:626 — the only SweepPoint push/emit — is skipped entirely. No point, no error: drained points has fewer entries than rpm_list and the done summary reports n_completed < n_rpms with no explanation. run_sweep_job (runner.rs:419-462) does not validate n_cycles_max > 0. run_single_rpm_inline handles the analogous case correctly at runner.rs:760 via .ok_or_else(|| 'no cycles completed at rpm {rpm}').
bugs.fix: When last_cs is None for an RPM, set error_state/stop with a message mirroring run_single_rpm_inline's 'no cycles completed at rpm {rpm}' Err, or at minimum emit a diagnostic so the missing point is explained rather than silently dropped.

bugs.title: compare alignment_key collision silently drops trials via BTreeMap overwrite
bugs.description: Trials are inserted into a_by_key/b_by_key BTreeMaps keyed by alignment_key(t), built only from (rpm, overrides) and excluding trial_id (compare.rs:34-41). BTreeMap::insert silently overwrites on key collision, so any two trial rows sharing the same rpm + canonicalized overrides collapse into one entry — all but the last are dropped from both the aligned diff and the unmatched listing, with no warning. Blast radius is currently limited because run.rs/sweep.rs always emit a numeric rpm and the DOE sampler normally yields distinct overrides, but duplicate sample rows or hand-authored/schema-divergent NDJSON (falling back to rpm='?' overrides='{}') trigger it. numeric_metric_keys explicitly skips trial_id (compare.rs:167), confirming trial_id is not part of the alignment identity.
bugs.fix: Include trial_id (or row index) in the alignment key, or detect a collision on insert (check contains_key before insert) and emit a warning / treat colliding rows as unmatched rather than overwriting.

bugs.title: PDM/SW-parser correctness and DoS hardening cluster: client-clock lock timestamp, unbounded property-value match, and uncapped deflate-decode attempts
bugs.description: Merged 3 low-severity PDM/parser findings (distinct root causes but same module cluster, all low, none release-gating). (1) release_lock writes released_at = chrono::Utc::now() computed on the untrusted client clock and PATCHes it directly (locks.rs:23-25,59-84, with a self-acknowledging TODO at :61); a skewed/manipulated clock makes audit lock-lifecycle ordering non-monotonic across clients. (2) extract_props_in (sw_properties.rs:380-399) takes a property value from the FIRST '<vt:' anywhere in the remaining text (no </property> boundary), so a self-closing <property name="X"/> preceding a valued <property name="Y">...val</vt:> can bind X to Y's value -> a data-card field shows the wrong value. (3) scan_region (sw_properties.rs:97-127,276-302) calls try_inflate at ~every byte offset of up to ~24M bytes with no cap on the NUMBER of inflate attempts, no wall-clock budget, and no cumulative-decompressed-bytes cap (only 64 MiB per single attempt) — an adversarial .sldprt/.sldasm with overlapping near-valid deflate framings is an O(file_size)-decode CPU/time self-DoS that can wedge a worker thread and stall check-in (no RCE/data loss; runs on spawn_blocking so the UI thread is safe).
bugs.fix: (1) Assign released_at server-side via RPC or DB trigger (now()) and stop sending a client-computed timestamp. (2) Bound the '<vt:' search to the current property element: locate the next </property> or next <property name=" and only search before it; if none, treat the property as value-less and skip. (3) Add a per-file cap on inflate attempts plus a wall-clock budget and a cumulative-decompressed-bytes cap, with a cheap pre-gate (plausible deflate block-header check or only attempting at container record-framing offsets).

patterns: Inconsistent panic-isolation wiring across the three CFD run paths: sweep and inline wrap eng.advance_one_cycle in run_engine_unwind_safe + SilencedPanicHook, but single-RPM (runner.rs:340) does not, and the Tauri dispatch lacks catch_unwind so an unwind skips the terminal status write — the asymmetry is the root of the critical job-wedge bug.

Pervasive index/unwrap on untrusted config JSON without bounds or schema checks (loader.rs r[0]/r[1], runner_lengths[0], firing_order/.as_i64().unwrap(); valve.rs ld_table[0] / len()-1 underflow): user-controlled config files panic the whole process at load/run time instead of returning ConfigLoadError::Schema. The correct req_f64/req_u and r.len() patterns already exist in the same file but weren't applied uniformly.

Hardcoded comma delimiter assumption throughout the helios-csv MoTeC/Link preamble path (dedupe_csv_header, count_csv_cells, parse_units_line all build default-comma csv readers): a single root cause producing a hard load failure AND unit-hint loss for non-US-locale vendor exports.

Missing input-field traversal/validation guards that a sibling function already implements: cfd_load_capture omits the job_id ../slash/backslash + path_under check that load_waves_from_dir performs — a known guard pattern simply not applied at one call site.

Silent data drop with no error surfaced when an expected entry is absent (sweep worker skips the SweepPoint push when last_cs is None; compare BTreeMap::insert overwrites on alignment_key collision): results are quietly incomplete with n_completed < expected and no diagnostic.

Default-deny / non-LIFO-safe handling of process-global state under concurrency: SilencedPanicHook take_hook/set_hook save-restore is only LIFO-correct intra-job but CfdState::register allows different-kind jobs to run concurrently, so the global panic hook can be corrupted to a permanent no-op.

Trusting the untrusted client and untrusted file content: release_lock uses the client wall clock for an audit timestamp, and the SW parser inflate scan has no per-file attempt/time/bytes budget against adversarial files.

domainTriage.summary: Triaged 7 verified database findings down to 5 distinct bugs (one merge of 3 is_admin()-scoping vulnerabilities). The dominant systemic issue is that pdm.is_admin() has no vault_id filter, so per-vault admins satisfy global-admin gates across multiple RPCs (delete/update/list users) — a flaw class the team already recognized as "M6" and fixed for audit_log in 20260619000400 but never back-ported. A second recurring pattern is delete-path attribution/scoping fixes (force_released_by, deleted_at guards, ancestor re-anchoring, soft-delete-aware probes) that were applied to the single-file/restore paths in the 0619 migrations but not back-ported to their sibling functions (delete_folder, reresolve_refs, add_and_lock resurrect, import_version). The top release-gate concern is the critical-tier privilege escalation allowing a per-vault admin to globally delete any non-admin user account.

bugs.title: pdm.is_admin() lacks vault_id filter: per-vault admins pass global-admin gates in admin_delete_user, admin_update_user, list_vault_roles, and admin_list_users
bugs.description:
Shared root cause: pdm.is_admin() (20260529000000 L38-41) tests role in ('owner','admin') with NO vault_id filter, so a role='admin', vault_id=<X> row (a per-vault admin, legitimately mintable by an owner via set_user_role) satisfies every gate that calls is_admin() without scope. This affects multiple privileged RPCs:
- admin_delete_user (20260618000100 L25, `if not pdm.is_admin()`): a per-vault admin can permanently and irreversibly delete ANY non-admin user's auth.users row (L59) and null/reassign all their FKs across pdm/pm/support org-wide. Target guards only check the TARGET's global role, never the caller's scope. This is the highest-impact, irreversible, destructive escalation — drives the merged entry to critical.
- admin_update_user (20260619000100 L26): a per-vault admin can overwrite any non-admin user's display_name/subteam globally (reversible).
- list_vault_roles (20260618000900 L32, `is_admin() or is_admin_in(p_vault_id)`): the is_admin() disjunct admits any per-vault admin for ANY p_vault_id, leaking emails/display_name/subteam/roles of vaults they have no role in.
- admin_list_users (20260531000000 L~263, `if not pdm.is_admin()`): returns the entire org-wide user list with emails to a per-vault admin (cross-vault PII disclosure).
The team explicitly recognized this exact flaw class as M6 and fixed it for audit_log in 20260619000400 by inlining a `vault_id IS NULL` predicate, but never back-ported it to these four functions. rls-audit-log-scoping.test.ts L109-131 proves per-vault admins are creatable and passed the old is_admin().
bugs.fix: Introduce a pdm.is_global_admin() helper: `exists(select 1 from pdm.user_roles where user_id = auth.uid() and role in ('owner','admin') and vault_id is null)`, mirroring the inline predicate from 20260619000400. Replace `if not pdm.is_admin()` with the global-only check in admin_delete_user (L25), admin_update_user (L26), and admin_list_users. For list_vault_roles, change only the first disjunct to is_global_admin() so cross-vault listing requires a global admin while per-vault admins retain access to their own vault via is_admin_in(p_vault_id). Add regression tests asserting a per-vault admin is rejected from each of these RPCs against another vault / global target.

bugs.title: delete_folder force-releases other users' locks with no force_released_by attribution and no force_unlock audit row
bugs.description: pdm.delete_folder (SECURITY DEFINER, live/never-superseded definition) soft-deletes a folder and releases every active subtree lock with a blanket `update pdm.locks set released_at = now() where released_at is null and file_id in (...)` (L65-69). It does NOT set force_released_by on displaced lock rows and writes NO per-holder force_unlock audit_log entry — only a single 'delete'/'folder' audit row. delete_file (20260619000600 L37-66) was explicitly given this attribution (loops over locks held by user_id <> v_caller, stamps force_released_by, inserts a per-holder 'force_unlock'/'lock' audit row), but delete_folder — which can displace many more holders at once — was never given the same treatment. force_released_total in vault_insights_extra and per-lock force-unlock history depend on force_released_by being set, so displaced checkouts look like voluntary check-ins and forced-unlock counts under-report. Same back-port-gap pattern as the is_admin() cluster.
bugs.fix: Mirror the 20260619000600 delete_file pattern in delete_folder: before the blanket release, loop over active subtree locks held by user_id <> v_caller, set released_at = now() and force_released_by = v_caller on each, and insert a 'force_unlock'/'lock' audit row per displaced holder (payload via='delete_folder', file_id, displaced_holder), each wrapped in begin/exception when others then null; then release remaining caller-owned locks as today.

bugs.title: reresolve_refs_for_file trigger re-resolves refs owned by soft-deleted parent assemblies (missing pf.deleted_at guard)
bugs.description: pdm.reresolve_refs_for_file() (latest definition; fires AFTER INSERT and AFTER UPDATE OF latest_version_id) re-resolves dangling child refs by unique basename. Its UPDATE joins pdm.versions pv -> pdm.files pf but filters only `pf.vault_id = new.vault_id` and `r.child_file_id is null` (L97-102) — it does NOT filter `pf.deleted_at is null`. The sibling deleted_at trigger handle_file_deleted_at_change (20260619000300 L83) deliberately added `and pf.deleted_at is null` for exactly this case (labeled M-3: don't re-resolve refs owned by a soft-deleted PARENT assembly), but the guard was never back-ported here. Result: when a child file is created/first published, refs belonging to a soft-deleted (recycle-bin) parent assembly get child_file_id/child_version_id re-populated, resurrecting Where-Used links for a recycled assembly. Low impact: tree/insights filter deleted parents, but direct refs reads for a restored child can momentarily show a deleted parent as a live consumer.
bugs.fix: Add `and pf.deleted_at is null` to the UPDATE ... FROM pdm.versions pv join pdm.files pf predicate in reresolve_refs_for_file(), matching the M-3 guard already present in handle_file_deleted_at_change().

bugs.title: add_and_lock resurrect path does not re-anchor soft-deleted ancestor folders (resurrected file orphaned from browse tree)
bugs.description: When add_and_lock re-adds a name occupied by a soft-deleted tombstone, the resurrect branch (L66-75) clears deleted_at/deleted_by and re-acquires a lock but does NOT re-anchor soft-deleted ANCESTOR folders the way restore_file does (20260619000200 BUG H4, L62-78: walk the folder_id parent_id chain clearing deleted_at on any soft-deleted ancestor, bounded against cycles). If an ancestor folder is still soft-deleted, the file becomes live but its folder_id points at a deleted folder, so useFolders/the browse tree (which excludes deleted folders) hides it despite the RPC returning a valid file_id/lock_id. Secondary edge case: the branch leaves published_at/created_by untouched, so resurrecting another user's never-published draft can return a file the caller cannot SELECT under files_read RLS until check-in publishes. Recoverable by restoring the folder; uncommon delete/re-add sequence.
bugs.fix: In the resurrect branch, after clearing deleted_at on the file, reuse the bounded ancestor re-anchor loop from restore_file (20260619000200) to clear deleted_at on soft-deleted ancestor folders. Optionally stamp created_by = v_caller / publish on resurrect so the resurrecting user can always see the row.

bugs.title: import_version idempotency probe ignores soft-deleted files (chains versions onto invisible tombstones)
bugs.description: pdm.import_version (service_role only; live definition, not redefined later) probes for an existing file by (vault_id, folder_id, name) WITHOUT filtering deleted_at (L53-57). If a file with that name was soft-deleted, re-importing finds the tombstoned row and chains the new version onto it (L59-99), leaving deleted_at set (invisible) rather than resurrecting it or treating it as a fresh import. add_and_lock was given explicit soft-delete awareness (20260618000300 L39 adds `and f.deleted_at is null` plus a resurrect branch); import_version was never updated — same back-port gap. Bulk re-imports/migrations touching a previously-deleted name append history to an invisible file; content never appears in the tree. Service-role/system path, not user-exploitable; silent data-visibility bug on re-runs.
bugs.fix: Add `and deleted_at is null` to the idempotency probe and, on a matching deleted row, resurrect it (clear deleted_at/deleted_by) before appending the version, mirroring add_and_lock's resurrect path; or skip with a clear status so the importer is aware.

patterns: is_admin() not vault-scoped (M6 flaw class): pdm.is_admin() has no vault_id filter, so per-vault admins satisfy global-admin gates across admin_delete_user, admin_update_user, list_vault_roles, and admin_list_users — needs a single is_global_admin() helper used everywhere a global operation is gated.

0619-fix-not-back-ported to sibling functions: attribution/guard/soft-delete fixes landed on the single-file or restore paths (delete_file force_released_by, handle_file_deleted_at_change M-3 deleted_at guard, restore_file ancestor re-anchor, add_and_lock soft-delete probe) but were never carried over to their counterparts (delete_folder, reresolve_refs_for_file, add_and_lock resurrect branch, import_version).

Missing soft-delete (deleted_at) awareness: multiple RPCs/triggers fail to filter or re-anchor on deleted_at, causing tombstoned/orphaned rows to resurface or be chained onto (reresolve_refs, add_and_lock resurrect, import_version).
Forced-unlock attribution gaps undercount vault_insights_extra.force_released_total and erase the displaced-holder audit trail (delete_folder).
Caller-scope vs target-scope confusion: privilege gates repeatedly check the TARGET's role but never the CALLER's vault scope (admin_delete_user, admin_update_user).

domainTriage.summary: Three distinct, verified native-integration (SOLIDWORKS add-in + sw-helper) bugs, no duplicates to merge. All are confined to the .NET interop layer and none is a hard release blocker. The highest-impact is a resource/lifetime leak (Task Pane control never disposed) that accumulates orphaned WinForms timers + GDI handles and keeps polling the localhost bridge every 4s after disconnect/reload. The other two are self-healing or degradation-only edge cases: a Vault tree branch that can wedge on 'Loading…' after an unguarded await throws (recoverable via Refresh), and a read-only flip in sw-helper that exact-matches normalized path strings and silently no-ops on divergent UNC/mapped/8.3 path forms (on-disk read-only bit is still the real guard). Recurring theme: managed-lifetime/cleanup wiring is incomplete on the teardown and error paths (no Dispose on disconnect, no finally to reset loading state, brittle exact-string path comparison).

bugs.title: Hosted Task Pane control is never disposed on add-in disconnect — leaks a 4s polling timer (orphaned WinForms control + GDI handles) for the life of the SOLIDWORKS process
bugs.description: DisconnectFromSW() (SwAddin.cs:152) sets `_control = null` without calling `_control.Dispose()`. HeliosVaultControl is hosted in the task pane only by HWND (DisplayWindowFromHandlex64, SwAddin.cs:84), so SOLIDWORKS does not own its managed lifetime and DeleteView() does not dispose it. The control Start()s a System.Windows.Forms.Timer (_pollTimer, Interval=4000) whose Tick handler polls the localhost bridge (HeliosVaultControl.cs:62-68); a running WinForms Timer's Tick delegate roots the control, so the GC.Collect()/WaitForPendingFinalizers() at SwAddin.cs:158-159 cannot reclaim it. The control's own Dispose(bool) (HeliosVaultControl.cs:72-80), which Stops/Disposes _pollTimer and disposes VaultTreePanel's ImageList, is never invoked. Confirmed: SwAddin.cs:152 is `_control = null;` with no Dispose.
bugs.fix: In DisconnectFromSW, before `_control = null;` (and before GC.Collect), call `_control?.Dispose();` so the existing Dispose override stops/disposes _pollTimer and disposes VaultTreePanel's ImageList. This stops the leaked HTTP poll and reclaims the orphaned control + GDI handles, and is correct across repeated enable/disable/reload cycles.

bugs.title: Vault tree branch wedges permanently on 'Loading…' if the first /files call throws (unguarded ReadAsStringAsync await), recoverable only via header Refresh
bugs.description: OnBeforeExpand sets `_vaultLoading = true` (VaultTreePanel.cs:218) then awaits LoadVaultModel(). FilesAsync can throw because HeliosBridge.SendAsync wraps ReadDiscovery and Http.SendAsync in try/catch (HeliosBridge.cs:90-97) but `await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()` (HeliosBridge.cs:102) is OUTSIDE that catch and can fault on a mid-read connection drop. The throw propagates into OnBeforeExpand's catch{} AFTER _vaultLoading=true but BEFORE _model is assigned, so the retry guard (`_model == null && !_vaultLoading`, line 216) is false forever and the branch never retries on expand. Verified: HeliosBridge.cs:102 ReadAsStringAsync sits after the catch that ends at :97.
bugs.fix: Reset `_vaultLoading = false` in a finally block in OnBeforeExpand (or LoadVaultModel) so a thrown FilesAsync leaves the branch retryable on the next expand. Optionally also wrap the ReadAsStringAsync await in HeliosBridge.SendAsync's existing try/catch so a mid-read drop returns Unreachable instead of throwing.
