bugs.title: sw-helper read-only flip matches by exact normalized path string — divergent UNC/mapped-drive/8.3 path forms silently no-op
bugs.description: The helper gates the in-session read-only flip on exact normalized string equality (`Norm(path) != target`, Program.cs:46), where Norm() only does slash-flip/trim/ToLowerInvariant (Program.cs:66-67). If SOLIDWORKS reports an open document's path in a textually different form than the desktop app passes (mapped drive Z:\ vs UNC \\server\share, or 8.3 short names), the loop skips it and returns exit 0 ('nothing to do'), so the caller treats it as success. The on-disk read-only bit (set by the desktop app, per the header at Program.cs:19-21) remains the real guard, so this is UX degradation (doc stays read-only after check-out / editable after check-in until reload), not data loss. Trigger depends on real-world path-form divergence, unproven here — hence low confidence.
bugs.fix: Compare by canonical full path (GetFinalPathNameByHandle / file identity) rather than raw lowercased string equality, and/or fall back to a filename match when no exact path match is found, so mapped/UNC/8.3 variants of the same file are recognized.

patterns: Incomplete managed-lifetime/cleanup on teardown paths: native-hosted controls are released by handle but never Dispose()d, leaking timers + GDI handles (SwAddin.DisconnectFromSW).
Loading/in-flight state flags set before an await but not reset in a finally, so a thrown async call leaves UI permanently wedged (VaultTreePanel _vaultLoading).

Unguarded awaits in the bridge layer: only SendAsync is wrapped, while ReadAsStringAsync (the actual mid-read failure point) is outside the try/catch, letting transient connection drops propagate as exceptions.
Brittle path identity: exact normalized-string equality instead of canonical/file-identity comparison, so equivalent UNC/mapped/8.3 path forms are treated as different files.

allConfirmed.title: Malformed sweep import (missing lastCycle) crashes torque-curve / summary / fuel-map readers
allConfirmed.description: studyFromBundle()'s sweep branch reconstructs SweepPoint objects from raw JSON and defensively guards ONLY the `cycles` array (line 78: `cycles: Array.isArray(p.cycles) ? p.cycles : []`). It does NOT validate that each point carries a `lastCycle` object, yet `lastCycle: CycleStats` is a required (non-optional) field on SweepPoint (state/types.ts:216). Every downstream sweep consumer dereferences `p.lastCycle.<field>` with no guard: torqueCurveFromSweep maps `p.lastCycle.brakeTorqueNm` BEFORE its Number.isFinite filter (lib/performance/torqueCurve.ts:20), peakOf/summarizeSweep/powerbandWidth read `p.lastCycle.brakePowerKW`/`brakeTorqueNm`/`veAtm`/`knockIntegral` (lib/analytics/sweepStats.ts:89,93,148,152-154), and fuelMapFromSweep reads `p.lastCycle.indicatedPowerKW`/`brakePowerKW`/`intakeMassPerCycleG` (lib/performance/fuelMap.ts:44-47). A hand-edited or corrupt bundle whose results.points entry omits `lastCycle` yields a SweepPoint with `lastCycle === undefined`.
allConfirmed.impact: Importing such a bundle and then selecting that sweep as a torque-curve / lap-sim source or opening it on the Sweep/Performance screen throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading brakeTorqueNm/brakePowerKW/indicatedPowerKW)' and crashes the CFD render, instead of the per-study skip-with-warning the importer was designed to emit.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: In studyFromBundle's sweep branch, drop or reject points lacking a usable lastCycle (e.g. filter on `isObj(p.lastCycle)`, or throw a per-study 'corrupt sweep point' warning so the bundle is skipped, matching the existing skip-with-warning contract). Alternatively make torqueCurveFromSweep/peakOf/fuelMapFromSweep null-safe on `lastCycle`.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: importStudy.ts:78 guards only `cycles`; types.ts:216 declares `lastCycle: CycleStats` (required); torqueCurve.ts:20 `({ rpm: p.rpm, torqueNm: p.lastCycle.brakeTorqueNm })` runs in .map() before the .filter, so it throws on undefined lastCycle. Downstream paths in description were originally cited as lib/torqueCurve.ts etc.; actual paths are lib/performance/ and lib/analytics/. Bug site (importStudy.ts) was cited correctly.

allConfirmed.title: Result screens keep stale local UI state when the active study changes (no remount key)
allConfirmed.description: ResultsScreen renders <SingleRpmResults>/<SweepResults>/<OptimizationResults> with only study={activeStudy} and no key (lines 26-31), and CfdHome renders <ResultsScreen /> without a key (CfdHome.tsx:114). The reducer's setActiveStudy only swaps activeStudyId (CfdContext.tsx:111-112). Switching between two studies of the SAME kind reconciles the same component instance, so all useState persists across the switch: in SweepResults dynoError/dynoWarn/expandedRpm/waveViewerRpm (SweepResults.tsx:78-81), and in OptimizationResults selectedIdx/sweepSeedTrial/paramForScatter/sortKey/sortDir/rankDim (OptimizationResults.tsx:83-93). paramForScatter is seeded once from study.parameterPaths[0] and the scatter filter Number.isFinite(t.parameterValues[paramForScatter]) (OptimizationResults.tsx:346) drops every trial when study B lacks that path, rendering an empty chart with a stale axis label.
allConfirmed.impact: After switching to a different study of the same kind the user can see a leftover dyno import error/warning banner from the previous study, a row left expanded, or an empty value-vs-parameter scatter bound to a parameter path that does not exist in the new study — UI that belongs to the previous study with no error surfaced.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Give each rendered results component a key tied to the study id, e.g. return <SweepResults key={activeStudy.id} study={activeStudy} /> (and likewise for the other kinds), forcing a clean remount + state reset on every study switch.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: ResultsScreen.tsx:29 `return <SweepResults study={activeStudy} />;` (no key); CfdContext.tsx:112 `return { ...s, activeStudyId: a.id };` (only id swapped); SweepResults.tsx:78-81 local useState; confirmed no remount.

allConfirmed.title: Dyno CSV import mis-parses thousands-grouped integers as decimal commas (~1000x corruption)
allConfirmed.description: parseNum() treats any cell matching /^-?\d+,\d+$/ as a European decimal comma and does cell.replace(',', '.'). That regex also matches a US thousands-grouped integer with no decimal point, e.g. '10,000' or '1,234'. The delimiter is chosen as whichever splits the header into the most columns (line 65-66), so for a semicolon- or tab-delimited dyno export the comma is NOT the field delimiter and a value like '10,000' survives as a single cell, then becomes Number('10.000') = 10.
allConfirmed.impact: Importing a tab/semicolon-delimited dyno export that uses comma thousands separators silently corrupts rpm/power/torque values by ~1000x (10,000 rpm -> 10). The dyno overlay and the on-screen RMSE/bias vs the sim are then computed against garbage with no error surfaced. The failure is format-dependent and silent.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Disambiguate before converting: when a cell contains exactly one comma followed by exactly three digits and no dot, treat it as a thousands group (strip the comma) rather than a decimal; only treat the comma as a decimal point when the fractional group length is not 3 (or detect locale once from all cells).
allConfirmed.verifier_note: importDyno.ts:54 `if (/^-?\d+,\d+$/.test(cell)) return Number(cell.replace(",", "."));` — '10,000' matches and yields Number('10.000')=10; delimiter picked at line 65-66 so comma can be a non-delimiter.

allConfirmed.title: buildSweepCyclesCsv / buildOptimizationCurvesCsv are rebuilt twice per export menu construction
allConfirmed.description: sweepActions() calls buildSweepCyclesCsv(study) at line 88 only to decide whether to push the action, then the action's run() at line 93 calls it again to produce the CSV. Same pattern for buildOptimizationCurvesCsv (lines 120 and 125). The presence-check materialises the full CSV string eagerly every time the export menu is built. In SweepResults the menu is memoised on [study, summary] (SweepResults.tsx:247), so it recomputes on every study object change — i.e. each new point appended during a live run — doing redundant O(rows) string building.
allConfirmed.impact: On large or live studies the export-menu memo does redundant full-CSV string building on every study update, adding avoidable GC/CPU churn during a run. Not a hang at normal sizes, but wasteful.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Build the CSV once and branch on null: const cyclesCsv = buildSweepCyclesCsv(study); if (cyclesCsv != null) actions.push({ ..., run: () => saveTextFile(`${stem}-cycles`, 'csv', cyclesCsv) }); same for the curves CSV.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: exportStudy.ts:88 `if (buildSweepCyclesCsv(study) != null)` then line 93 `const csv = buildSweepCyclesCsv(study);` — same builder called twice; SweepResults.tsx:247 memo deps `[study, summary]`.

allConfirmed.title: Lap-channel CSV provenance comments interpolate config/vehicle/track names without escaping
allConfirmed.description: The leading '#'-prefixed comment lines embed meta.configName, meta.vehicleName and meta.trackName directly via template strings (lines 38-40) with no CR/LF stripping or quoting, unlike the numeric data rows (which are all toFixed/String of numbers and need no escaping). A newline in configName/vehicleName/trackName would split the comment preamble into what looks like an extra row, and an embedded comma changes the apparent field structure of the header block.
allConfirmed.impact: A config/vehicle/track name containing a newline (or comma) produces a malformed CSV preamble — an extra apparent row or a comment that bleeds into the data block — which can confuse downstream Excel/MATLAB/MoTeC importers. Names are user-influenceable (config filenames, vehicle config name), though not free-form attacker input today.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Strip CR/LF (and ideally collapse commas) from the interpolated names before embedding, mirroring the cell-sanitising discipline used for the rest of the export layer.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: lapChannelsCsv.ts:38 `# config: ${meta.configName}` etc., no sanitisation; data rows (lines 51-66) are numeric-only so the asymmetry is real.

allConfirmed.title: CycleChart: `new uPlot(...)` not wrapped in try-catch — degenerate data crashes the component
allConfirmed.description: CycleChart calls `plotRef.current = new uPlot(opts, data, plotHostRef.current)` at line 109 with no try-catch, and `plotRef.current.setData(data)` at line 126 with no try-catch. LinePlot wraps both equivalent calls in try-catch (lines 225-234 and 249-253). uPlot throws on degenerate data shapes. Because both calls are inside layout/data effects, an unhandled exception propagates upward and unmounts the results page.
allConfirmed.impact: If cycles is transiently empty or has mismatched series count during study loading, the Single-RPM or Sweep results page crashes with a white screen.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap the `new uPlot(...)` call at line 109 in a try-catch identical to LinePlot lines 225-234. Wrap `plotRef.current.setData(data)` at line 126 in a try-catch identical to LinePlot lines 249-253. Set `plotRef.current = null` on the construction catch so the setData effect short-circuits on the broken instance.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Line 109: `plotRef.current = new uPlot(opts, data, plotHostRef.current);` — no try-catch. Line 126: `plotRef.current.setData(data);` — no try-catch. LinePlot has `try { plotRef.current = new uPlot(...) } catch(e) { ... plotRef.current = null; }` at lines 225-234 and `try { plotRef.current?.setData(...) } catch(e) {...}` at lines 249-253.

allConfirmed.title: GGDiagram: longitudinal axis (`maxLong`) incorrectly floored against `muLat` instead of `muLong`

allConfirmed.title: folderPath / folderNamePath recurse with no cycle guard — a corrupt parent_id chain stack-overflows the renderer
allConfirmed.description: folderPath() (lines 51-58) and folderNamePath() (lines 78-84) walk the parent_id chain via unbounded self-recursion (`const parent = folderPath(f.parent_id, folders)`) with NO depth or cycle guard. A cyclic parent_id (A.parent=B, B.parent=A) or a self-parent makes folderPath/folderNamePath recurse forever and throw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. folderPath is on hot paths: vaultRelativePath (local-match.ts line 13, every sync match), localDestPath, vaultRelPathFor, so the whole vault UI becomes unopenable, not just one screen.

Because folderPath feeds vaultRelativePath/matchLocal, it crashes during routine sync matching, not just on one screen.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Rewrite both as an iterative walk with a `guard++ < 64` cap and/or a seen-id Set, returning the partial/truncated path on overflow — mirroring isDescendantOf / nearestLiveAncestor / resolveBreadcrumbPath in the same file, which already degrade gracefully against a corrupt chain.

allConfirmed.title: Unresolved-reference warning uses ilike with raw basename — `_`/`%` in filenames act as SQL wildcards, producing false 'ambiguous' warnings
allConfirmed.description: Line 57 counts vault files matching a child hint via `.ilike("name", base)` with the comment `// no wildcards → case-insensitive equality`. That comment is wrong: in PostgreSQL LIKE/ILIKE, `_` matches any single character and `%` matches any run of characters. The basename is taken verbatim from `r.child_path_hint` (line 50) and not escaped. CAD/part filenames very commonly contain underscores (e.g. `Bracket_01.SLDPRT`), so the ilike pattern over-matches (`BracketX01.SLDPRT`), inflating `count` and pushing `reason` from 'missing' to 'ambiguous' (line 58).
allConfirmed.impact: After check-in, files whose names merely contain an underscore can show the misleading 'reference matches multiple vault files (rename one to disambiguate)' warning (line 69) even with no real ambiguity. Warning-accuracy only (no data loss), eroding trust in the cross-reference health surface this code was added to provide.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Escape LIKE metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) in `base` before the ilike, or replace with a case-insensitive exact match (fetch names and compare lowercased). Fix the misleading comment on line 57.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: line 57 is `.ilike("name", base)` with `base` derived unescaped at line 50 (`r.child_path_hint.split(/[\\/]/).pop()`); ilike treats `_`/`%` as wildcards, so the `(count ?? 0) > 1` test at line 58 can falsely fire.

allConfirmed.title: useAutoAddDrafts can stall busy-skipped/cancelled candidates until an unrelated external trigger re-fires the effect
allConfirmed.description: The effect early-returns when `busyRef.current` is true (line 96). If deps (`unmatched`/`tick`) change while a run is in flight, the new effect run is dropped, and the old run's cleanup sets `cancelled = true` (line 143), which breaks the loop early (line 128). The finally (lines 137-140) clears `busyRef.current = false` but does NOT bump `tick` or otherwise re-arm the effect. The only self-retrigger in the hook is the `deferredFresh` setTick path (lines 120-122), which fires only for too-fresh files and is never reached on the busy early-return. So candidates deferred because a run was busy — or cut off by `cancelled` mid-loop — are not retried until `unmatched` or `tick` changes again from an unrelated source (a fresh scan or the STABLE_AGE timer).

allConfirmed.suggested_fix: In the finally, when a run ended with work left undone (cancelled mid-loop, or it never ran because busy), bump an internal tick to re-arm the effect — mirroring the existing deferredFresh setTick path.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: line 96 early-returns on busyRef; the finally at lines 137-140 resets busyRef/adding but never calls setTick; the only setTick re-arm (lines 120-122) is gated on deferredFresh and unreachable on the busy path.

allConfirmed.title: Vehicle mass total double-counts assembly rollup mass against its own parts
allConfirmed.description: aggregateMass() loops over every FileMassRow and adds extractMassGrams(file._properties) into totalGrams (line 118) and into the per-subsystem map (line 125) with no distinction between leaf parts (.SLDPRT) and assemblies (.SLDASM). SolidWorks stores a computed rollup Mass on assembly versions equal to the sum of its children, so every gram from a leaf part is counted again for each ancestor assembly that carries a Mass property. The sibling BOM code in the same library deliberately guards against exactly this: flattenBom sets effectiveMass = isAssembly ? null : node.massGrams (bom.ts:202-208) with a comment 'counting it here alongside the children's masses would double-count every gram already contributed by the leaf parts below.' aggregateMass has no equivalent guard. withMassCount/missingCount and the heaviest[] ranking can legitimately include assemblies, but totalGrams and bySubsystem are inflated.
allConfirmed.impact: The headline Vehicle Mass KPI and the weight-budget over/under-target delta on the MassPanel are inflated whenever the vault contains assemblies that carry a Mass custom property (the SolidWorks default). For nested vehicle assemblies the inflation compounds at each sub-assembly level, so the reported total can be 2x or more the true mass, directly misleading the weight-budget feature.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Exclude assembly rollup mass from totalGrams and bySubsystem the same way bom.ts does: skip files whose name ends in .SLDASM (or whose type is assembly), or pass the BOM graph in and only sum leaf parts (no child refs). Keep assemblies in the heaviest[] ranking for display if desired.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: massStats.ts:118 'totalGrams += massGrams;' runs for every file with no leaf/assembly guard, while bom.ts:208 'const effectiveMass = isAssembly ? null : node.massGrams;' suppresses it; the test fixture sums 'Chassis_Main.SLDASM' (1,200 g) into the 5000 g total (massStats.test.ts:109,128-129) and into the Chassis subsystem (test.ts:156).

allConfirmed.title: Notification dedup id embeds receive-time timestamp, so re-delivered events are not de-duplicated
allConfirmed.description: makeId() builds the id as `${table}:${eventType}:${rowId}:${at}` (line 78) and its own doc comment claims this makes the id deterministic 'so that replaying the same event twice de-dupes cleanly.' But `at` is not derived from the event row; it is stamped at receive time by the hook via `const at = new Date().toISOString()` (useNotifications.ts:109) and passed into eventToNotification, which embeds it in every makeId call (lines 122, 146, 186, 222). mergeNotifications() is the only dedup point and keys solely on id (notifications.ts:251-253). If the realtime channel re-delivers the same postgres_changes event (e.g. after a websocket reconnect/resubscribe), the second delivery gets a different wall-clock `at`, hence a different id, and is treated as a brand-new notification. The unit tests pass a fixed AT constant, masking the issue.
allConfirmed.impact: After a websocket reconnect or resubscribe, a single check-in/check-out/unlock/delete event can appear as a duplicate notification with an inflated unread count. The de-dup guarantee the module advertises does not hold for the exact replay case it was designed for.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the dedup component of the id from stable event-row data (e.g. the version row id, lock id, or the row's created_at/released_at/deleted_at from newRow) rather than the caller-supplied receive-time `at`. Keep `at` only as the display timestamp field, not as part of the id.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: notifications.ts:78 returns `${table}:${eventType}:${rowId}:${at}` and useNotifications.ts:109 sets `const at = new Date().toISOString();` at receive time; mergeNotifications dedups only by id (notifications.ts:251 'new Set(incoming.map((n) => n.id))').

allConfirmed.title: Property-aware search makes filename matching case-sensitive when prop: tokens are present
allConfirmed.description: In VaultSearch the scoring needle is chosen as `const scoreText = hasPropFilters ? parsed.text : rawQ.toLowerCase()` (line 76). parsed.text comes from parseSearchQuery, which preserves the original case of free-text tokens (propertySearch.ts:82 pushes m[5] with no .toLowerCase()). score() (VaultSearch.tsx:19-30) lowercases only the filename (`const n = name.toLowerCase()`) and then compares it against the raw needle via `n.indexOf(q)` and `ch === q[i]`. So when the query contains any prop: token, a mixed-case free-text term can never substring/subsequence-match the lowercased filename. The propertyTextMatch path (lines 90-93) only checks property VALUES, not filenames, so it does not rescue a filename-only term. Without prop tokens the rawQ.toLowerCase() path works, so the defect is specific to combined queries like 'Frame prop:Material=7075'. Root cause is split across propertySearch.ts (free text never lowercased) and the consuming component.
allConfirmed.impact: A user combining a capitalized filename term with a property filter (the documented `bracket prop:Material=steel` use case) gets zero filename matches unless they type the term all-lowercase. The feature silently under-returns results, making property-aware search look broken for any capitalized filename query.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Lowercase the free-text needle before scoring, e.g. `const scoreText = (hasPropFilters ? parsed.text : rawQ).toLowerCase();`, or lowercase q at the top of score(). matchesProperties/propertyTextMatch already lowercase internally, so only filename scoring is affected.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: VaultSearch.tsx:76 'const scoreText = hasPropFilters ? parsed.text : rawQ.toLowerCase();' uses un-lowercased parsed.text; propertySearch.ts:82 'textTokens.push(m[5]);' never lowercases; score() compares lowercased name 'n.indexOf(q)' (VaultSearch.tsx:20-21) against the raw needle. NOTE: cited file is under components/, not lib/, though the lib propertySearch.ts is part of the root cause.

allConfirmed.title: CheckOutButton: re-click guard resets before confirm dialog closes, allowing concurrent checkout attempts
allConfirmed.description: In `handleClick`, the `finally` block (lines 158-161) unconditionally sets `checkingRef.current = false` and `setChecking(false)`. When a where-used warning is detected, the `try` block calls `setWhereUsedConfirm(warning.message)` and `return`s at line 153 — but `return` inside a `try` still executes `finally`. So by the time the confirm dialog is visible, `checkingRef.current` is already `false` and `checking` is `false`. The button re-enables and a second click can re-enter `handleClick`, fetch where-used again, and if the second fetch finds no warning, call `doCheckOut()` while the first dialog is still open. If the user then also confirms the first dialog, `doCheckOut()` fires a second time, resulting in two concurrent `acquireLock.run(fileId)` calls and potentially two locks or a duplicate RPC.
allConfirmed.impact: User can trigger two concurrent checkout attempts if they click the Check Out button again while the where-used confirmation dialog is open, potentially acquiring duplicate lock RPCs.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Do not reset `checkingRef.current` in `finally` when the early return is due to a where-used warning. Instead, track a separate `confirmPending` boolean and reset `checkingRef`/`checking` only after the dialog resolves (both `onConfirm` and `onClose` paths).
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: `finally { checkingRef.current = false; setChecking(false); }` at lines 158-161 always runs on the `return` at line 154, re-enabling the button while `whereUsedConfirm` state is set and the dialog is open.

allConfirmed.title: BulkActionBar: `bulkCancel` increments `fail` for restore failures even though lock was already released — success count undercounts
allConfirmed.description: After `releaseLock.run(id)` succeeds at line 319, the code attempts to restore the local file. If the restore download fails at line 329-331, it does `fail++; continue` without ever incrementing `ok`. The final status message at line 344 says `Cancelled ${ok}/N (fail failed)`, misreporting files whose vault-side lock WAS successfully released as failures. A user seeing '0/3 (3 failed)' when all three locks were released will retry the operation, causing redundant lock-release RPCs that will error ('no active lock') and confuse them further.

allConfirmed.title: BrowseScreen: `fileCountByFolder` recursive `count()` has no cycle guard — cyclic parent_id crashes with stack overflow
allConfirmed.description: The `count(id)` function at line 679 memoizes results in `total` using `if (cached !== undefined) return cached` — but the cache is only written at `total.set(id, n)` AFTER the recursive calls to `count(child)` return (line 684). With a cycle (folder A's parent_id = B, B's parent_id = A), `count(A)` starts, finds no cache entry, calls `count(B)`, which finds no cache entry and calls `count(A)` again — the in-progress A has not been written to `total` yet. This recurses infinitely until the JS stack overflows with a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`, crashing BrowseScreen. The sibling `selectedFiles` useMemo at line 421 handles cycles safely with an explicit stack/set; this function does not.
allConfirmed.impact: Any cyclic parent_id reference in the folders table (via bad migration, manual DB edit, or server bug) causes BrowseScreen to throw an unhandled RangeError and the entire vault Browse tab becomes unusable.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Write a sentinel (e.g. `total.set(id, 0)`) before recursing, or add a `visiting` Set and return 0 immediately when the id is already in it: `if (visiting.has(id)) return 0; visiting.add(id);`
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: `total.set(id, n)` is at line 684, AFTER `for (const child of byParent.get(id) ?? []) n += count(child)` at line 683 — a cycle hits `count(A)` recursively with A not yet present in `total`, giving infinite recursion.

allConfirmed.title: NotificationFeed: actor rendered as raw UUID prefix instead of display name
allConfirmed.description: Line 191 renders `by {n.actorId.slice(0, 8)}…` — an 8-character hex prefix of the actor's user UUID — for every notification item that has an actorId. The component receives no user-name map and has no resolution mechanism. allConfirmed.title: BrowseScreen: multi-file context-menu delete uses a single hook instance in a loop — last error clobbers earlier ones
allConfirmed.description: The `onConfirm` handler at line 1238 loops over `targetFiles` calling `deleteFile.run(f.id)` sequentially on the same shared `deleteFile` hook instance. The hook stores a single `.error` value that is overwritten by each call. At line 1250, the status message appends `deleteFile.error.message` — this reflects only the last failed RPC's error. allConfirmed.title: New-task creation races task INSERT against its dependency/extra-subteam inserts (FK violation, silent data loss)
allConfirmed.description: onSubmit calls onCreate(task) (the store's addTask) then immediately fires addTaskSubteam(task.id, ...) for each extra subteam and addDependency(...) for each prereq/dependent. Each store action issues its own independent fire-and-forget persist() write. There is no await/serialization between the task INSERT and the membership/dependency INSERTs, so insertTaskSubteam/insertDependency can reach Postgres before insertTask commits, violating the task_subteams.task_id / task_dependencies.*_id FK. The task row persists but the extra membership/dependency is rejected and rolled back, while the UI showed it optimistically — it silently vanishes on the next background refresh, plus a confusing FK error toast. addTask ALREADY persists extras in an ordered chain (insertTask first, then per-extra inserts) when they are passed via the task object, so the fix is to route extra subteams/dependencies through addTask's single persist rather than separate calls.
allConfirmed.impact: When a teammate creates a task with additional subteams or dependencies (a supported, reachable feature — the dialog has UI to stage both via extraSubteamIds/prereqIds/dependentIds), the extra membership/dependency can fail server-side with an FK error humanized as 'refers to something that no longer exists.' The relationship is lost silently after refresh and a spurious error toast appears on an otherwise-successful create.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Pass extraSubteamIds + dependency lists into addTask so a single persist() runs insertTask first and then the dependent inserts sequentially (the pattern addTask already uses for owners/extra subteams in the task object), or have addTask return an awaitable the dialog awaits before calling addTaskSubteam/addDependency.

Dialog passes subteams:[subteam] only (CreateTaskDialog.tsx:308) and calls addTaskSubteam separately (322-325).

allConfirmed.title: Bulk 'Due' date field clears due dates on ALL selected tasks when blurred while empty
allConfirmed.description: The bulk-edit Due <input type="date"> is uncontrolled (no value/defaultValue, starts empty) and onBlur unconditionally calls commitDue(e.currentTarget.value). commitDue('') maps to apply({ due_date: null }) which runs bulkUpdateTasks over every selected id. There is no guard that the user entered or changed a date, so merely focusing the field and clicking/tabbing away fires a blur with value '' and clears the due_date of every selected task.

allConfirmed.title: TaskDetailSheet auto-nulls subsystem via updateTask even when the user has no edit permission

If the sharing config is absent from this browser's localStorage it can repeatedly attempt to null a valid subsystem on every task/teamSubsystems change.

allConfirmed.title: Team-scoped onCreate re-homes the primary subteam but leaves the dialog-selected subteam as a stray secondary membership
allConfirmed.description: When a view is scoped to a subteam, onCreate builds teamPatched = { ...task, subteam_id: currentTeam.id, subteam: currentTeam, subsystem_id: null, subsystem: null } but does NOT overwrite task.subteams, which the dialog set to [the dialog-selected subteam]. allConfirmed.title: seedAnchor in CalendarViewClient is computed once with an empty dependency array

allConfirmed.title: TableViewClient renderRow creates new function closures on every render, preventing row-level bailout

allConfirmed.title: Leaderboard individual player ranks ignore ties — consecutive ranks assigned

allConfirmed.title: Retry submit can insert duplicate score rows on flaky network
allConfirmed.description: onRetrySubmit at line 114 calls handleGameOver(over.score) again, which executes a plain INSERT via submitScore. If the original request reached the DB but the response was lost in transit, the retry inserts a second identical row. allConfirmed.title: Module-level leaderboard cache never cleared on user sign-out

allConfirmed.title: Role Editor sends disabled-but-checked capabilities, so a manage-roles admin who lacks a cap cannot edit (even rename/recolor) any role that contains it
allConfirmed.description: In RoleCard, each capability checkbox is rendered checked={selected.has(c.key)} (line 1001) but disabled={locked || busy || !can(c.key)} (line 1002). `selected` is seeded from role.capabilities (line 941). A capability the editor does NOT personally hold (!can(c.key)) is shown disabled-yet-CHECKED and stays in `selected`. save() always sends [...selected] (line 972) to pm.upsert_role, whose server-side edit-subset guard requires the full capability array to be a subset of the caller's own caps and otherwise raises 'cannot define a role with capabilities you do not hold' (migration 20260617002000_pm_rbac_admin_rpcs.sql lines 130-135), rejecting the ENTIRE upsert. So a non-system role is presented as fully editable (locked = role.is_system || !canManage; only 'owner' is is_system) yet ANY save -- even just renaming or recoloring -- is rejected because the un-removable disabled cap is included. CORRECTION to the original finding: the cited Executive example is INVALID. Migration 20260617004000_pm_rbac_model_cleanup.sql lines 14-16 add org.manage_admins to the executive ROLE definition, so any user holding the Executive role DOES hold org.manage_admins and can edit every role. The real trigger is any CUSTOM role that grants org.manage_roles together with only a subset of caps: such a user can manage roles (canManage true) but lacks some caps, and is then unable to edit any role that contains those caps.

At minimum do not include disabled-but-checked caps the caller cannot toggle in a way that guarantees rejection.

Executive example refuted: migration 20260617004000 lines 14-16 grant executive org.manage_admins.

allConfirmed.title: useMyCapabilities never refetches, so self-/newly-granted permissions stay stale (gated controls remain disabled) until full app reload

allConfirmed.title: Grant dropdown offers subteam roles a subteam-only granter cannot actually grant (no grant-subset filtering client-side)

allConfirmed.title: Auto-provision trigger grants every open self-signup immediate global editor (write) access to the production vault, reopening the previously-fixed critical hole

Self-signup is open and instant: config.toml has enable_signup=true (lines 171, 216) and enable_confirmations=false (line 228), so signUp returns a session and AuthModal logs the user straight in (AuthModal.tsx lines 390-405); the anon key is distributed and treated as public (connection.ts lines 1-8; AuthModal.tsx lines 264-267). That assumption is now false: a fresh signup HAS a global editor row, which satisfies the storage SELECT policy (any role row -> list/download every vault object; 20260511000700 lines 39-42), the storage INSERT policy (role in admin/editor -> upload arbitrary bytes; lines 51-52), and pdm.can_edit_in for EVERY vault because that helper accepts vault_id IS NULL rows (20260531000000 lines 34-39: role in owner/admin/editor and (vault_id is null or vault_id = p_vault_id)). Change the baseline auto-provisioned role from 'editor' to 'viewer' (or a no-access 'pending' role) so a fresh account cannot upload/modify and an admin must promote; and/or gate signup with a before_user_created hook or email-domain allowlist plus email confirmation; and/or require admin approval before any role row is created. Update the now-false config.toml comment (lines 224-226) and the storage-RLS assumption so the access model is consistent.

allConfirmed.title: CSV export is vulnerable to spreadsheet formula injection via channel ids/units
allConfirmed.description: csvCell() quotes only cells containing [",\n]; it does not neutralize spreadsheet formula-injection prefixes (=, +, -, @, tab, CR). The export header row is built from channel ids (csv-export.ts:36 `metas.map(m => m.id)`) and units (line 42 `metas.map(m => m.units)`). For an unknown CSV column, the Rust registry synthesizes the channel id and display_name directly from the raw header text (helios-csv/src/registry.rs:158 `id: header.to_string()`) and units from the CSV unit row (registry.rs:152-153 `unit_hint.trim()`). So a CSV column header like `=HYPERLINK(...)` / `@SUM(...)` / `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` becomes a channel id and is written verbatim into row 1 of the Helios-generated export.

allConfirmed.title: derivative() divides by zero on duplicate adjacent timestamps, emitting non-finite spikes
allConfirmed.description: All three difference branches divide by a time delta with no zero-guard: forward at i=0 `(v1-v0)/(t1-t0)` (line 26), central in the interior `(values[i+1]-values[i-1])/(tp-tm)` (line 32), and backward at i=N-1 `(vN1-vN2)/(tN1-tN2)` (line 39). When neighboring sample times are equal (duplicated rows, or a low-resolution time column where timeUs[i-1]===timeUs[i+1]), the denominator is 0 and the output is +/-Infinity (or NaN when the numerator is also 0). The module's own contract (header comment lines 5-7) is to emit NaN for samples it can't compute, and the sibling ops integral/smooth/lowpass/highpass all guard their inputs — derivative is the outlier that emits non-finite spikes instead of gaps.
allConfirmed.impact: A math channel using derivative() over dirty CSV data with repeated timestamps produces Infinity/-Infinity spikes that poison downstream arithmetic (anything combined with them stays non-finite) and blow out auto-scaled chart y-axes, making the trace unreadable. Silently wrong output, not a crash.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Guard each delta: `const dt = t1 - t0; out[i] = dt !== 0 ? (v1 - v0)/dt : NaN;` for all three branches (forward, central, backward).
allConfirmed.verifier_note: vector-ops.ts:32 `out[i] = (values[i+1]! - values[i-1]!) / (tp - tm);` with no `tp !== tm` check; lines 26 and 39 identical pattern; contrast integral()/smooth()/lowpass() which all Number.isFinite-guard.

allConfirmed.title: lapAggregate per-lap accumulation includes the lap-end boundary sample, double-attributing it to adjacent laps
allConfirmed.description: Laps are defined and built as half-open intervals [startUs, endUs) and are contiguous (in buildLaps a trusted lap has startUs=crossings[i], endUs=crossings[i+1], so lap N's endUs == lap N+1's startUs). The per-lap accumulation loop uses `if (tUs < lap.startUs) continue; if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;`, so a sample whose timestamp equals lap.endUs is processed for lap N (the `>` test does not break on equality) AND for lap N+1 (its `tUs < lap.startUs` test is false at startUs). The value therefore contributes fully to lap N's max/min/mean/last and again to lap N+1's first/min/max/mean, and inflates lap_mean's denominator (cnt) in both. The broadcast loop below at line 514 uses the half-open test `tUs >= lap.endUs`, so the two halves use inconsistent boundary semantics. This is reachable for beacon and expression detection, where the crossing timestamp pushed (`out.push(tUs)` with tUs taken from an actual sample) exactly coincides with a real sample timestamp at the boundary.
allConfirmed.impact: lap_max/lap_min/lap_mean/lap_last for a lap can be skewed by a single boundary sample that belongs to the next lap; a boundary spike on an RPM/ITB trace can land in the wrong lap's readout, and lap_mean's denominator is off by one. Small, single-sample, user-visible per-lap statistic error.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Use the same half-open test as the broadcast loop: change `if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;` to `if (tUs >= lap.endUs) break;` in the per-lap accumulation loop.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: line 491 `if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;` vs broadcast line 514 `while (... tUs >= set.laps[li]!.endUs) li++;`; buildLaps lines 354-356 make laps contiguous so endUs==next startUs; beacon (line 283 `out.push(tUs)`) and expression (line 313) push actual sample timestamps, making the coincident-boundary case reachable.

allConfirmed.description: After the containing-lap scan fails, the tail fallback is `return tUs <= last.endUs ? set.laps.length - 1 : -1;`. This returns the LAST lap index for ANY tUs <= last.endUs, including any tUs strictly before laps[0].startUs (e.g. a cursor positioned before the session's first sample, or a manual-crossing config whose first lap does not start at the data origin). The sibling lapAt() (lines 145-146) does not have this defect because its tail fallback also requires `tUs >= last.startUs`. lapIndexAt is missing that lower bound, so the two functions disagree for the head-of-session case.

allConfirmed.title: Single-RPM solver panic is not isolated — worker thread unwinds, job stuck 'Running' forever, permanently blocking all future single-RPM studies

The sweep worker (line 533-535) and run_single_rpm_inline (line 727-729) both wrap the identical call in run_engine_unwind_safe and convert a caught panic into an ErrorReason::SolverDiverged event/Err. Per the module comment at lines 69-73, the SDM26 solver panic!s on positivity failure / junction non-convergence; DefaultDivergenceProbe only screens non-finite CycleStats AFTER a cycle completes and never sees a panic. The job runs in a bare std::thread::spawn closure (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/cfd/commands.rs:156) whose terminal status write is at lines 198-199 AFTER the run_* call, so an unwinding panic skips it and JobHandle.status stays Running. Sweep and optimization remain usable, making the asymmetry look like an oversight.

Additionally, wrap the run_* dispatch in commands.rs in catch_unwind so the terminal status is always recorded.

allConfirmed.title: Process-global panic hook save/restore races between concurrent jobs of different kinds, potentially leaving a permanent no-op hook
allConfirmed.description: SilencedPanicHook::install (line 105-109) calls process-global std::panic::take_hook() then set_hook(noop), and Drop (line 111-116) restores the saved hook. This is correct only under strict LIFO nesting. CfdState::register (state.rs:69-77) only rejects a NEW job whose kind matches an already-Running job — different kinds run concurrently, each in its own thread (commands.rs:156), and both the sweep (runner.rs:501) and optimization (runner.rs:985) paths execute `let _hook_guard = SilencedPanicHook::install()`. Interleaving: Sweep installs (saves REAL hook, sets noop) -> Optimization installs (saves the NOOP hook, sets noop) -> Sweep drops (restores REAL hook) -> Optimization drops (restores the NOOP hook). The process is then left with a permanent no-op panic hook. The doc comment at lines 99-100 claims installing once per pool.install 'avoids racing set_hook/take_hook across workers' — true only intra-job, giving false confidence; it does not address inter-job concurrency.

allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Do not use the process-global hook for per-region silencing when concurrent jobs are possible. Options: (a) serialize all CFD jobs through a global mutex so only one solver region runs at a time; (b) install a process-lifetime hook once at startup that filters solver panics via a thread-local/atomic 'in solver region' flag; or (c) reference-count installs under a global mutex so the real hook is saved once and restored only when the last region exits.

allConfirmed.title: Sweep worker silently drops an RPM (no point, no error) when zero cycles complete
allConfirmed.description: In the sweep worker, if the per-RPM cycle loop produces no CycleStats (n_cycles_max == 0 so `for cycle_i in 0..0` never runs, or the first advance_one_cycle returns TargetReached/Cancelled at lines 538-539 before any stats are pushed), `last_cs = accumulated.last().copied()` (line 600) is None and the `if let Some(last) = last_cs` block at line 626 is skipped entirely — no SweepPoint pushed, no error recorded. The drained `points` then has fewer entries than rpm_list and the done summary reports n_completed < n_rpms with no explanation. The sweep runner does not validate n_cycles_max > 0 (no guard in run_sweep_job lines 419-462). run_single_rpm_inline handles the analogous case correctly at line 760 via `.ok_or_else(|| format!("no cycles completed at rpm {rpm:.0}"))?`.
allConfirmed.impact: A sweep configured with n_cycles_max == 0 (or an RPM that immediately hits TargetReached) silently yields a result set missing that RPM with no error surfaced — the chart has a hole and n_completed is quietly lower than expected.

allConfirmed.title: Config loader panics on malformed Cd-table rows instead of returning a schema error
allConfirmed.description: unpack_cd_table checks each row is an array via row.as_array() but then indexes r[0] and r[1] directly. A Cd-table row with fewer than two elements (e.g. [0.05] or []) panics with index-out-of-bounds rather than returning ConfigLoadError::Schema. unpack_cd_table is called for both intake_valve.cd_table and exhaust_valve.cd_table on every load_v1_json call (lines 87-88), so any user/sweep config with a short row crashes the process at load time.
allConfirmed.impact: A user-supplied config file with a short/empty Cd-table row crashes the whole process (panic) at load time instead of surfacing a clean ConfigLoadError::Schema. In a sweep/optimization service this aborts the entire job rather than rejecting one config.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Check r.len() >= 2 (or use r.get(0)/r.get(1)) and return ConfigLoadError::Schema on a short row, mirroring the existing .ok_or_else handling already used for the as_f64() conversions on lines 52-53. Note the spark_advance_map loader at lines 264-269 already does exactly this (r.len() != 2 check) — applying the same pattern here is the fix.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Lines 52-53: `ld.push(r[0].as_f64()...)` / `cd.push(r[1].as_f64()...)` index r[0]/r[1] after only `row.as_array()` on line 49, with no r.len() check (contrast lines 266-269 which do guard r.len() != 2).

allConfirmed.title: Config loader panics on empty intake_pipes / exhaust_primaries arrays and non-array firing_order
allConfirmed.description: load_v1_json requires intake_pipes and exhaust_primaries to be arrays (lines 70-73) but never checks they are non-empty, then unconditionally indexes runner_lengths[0], runner_diameters_in[0], runner_wall_ts[0] (lines 119-123), primary_lengths[0], primaries[0] (lines 125-129). An empty array panics on [0]. Additionally line 90/95/97/101 use p["length"].as_f64().unwrap() and p["wall_temperature"].as_f64().unwrap(), and lines 115-116 use data["firing_order"].as_array().unwrap() with per-element .as_i64().unwrap(), all of which panic on missing/wrong-typed JSON fields instead of returning ConfigLoadError::Schema.

This is user-controlled input via the config file, so in a sweep/optimization service it aborts the whole job.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Validate intake_pipes/exhaust_primaries are non-empty before indexing [0], and replace p["length"].as_f64().unwrap() / p["wall_temperature"].as_f64().unwrap() / data["firing_order"].as_array().unwrap() / .as_i64().unwrap() with req_f64-style helpers returning ConfigLoadError::Schema (helpers req_f64/req_u already exist at lines 21-32).

allConfirmed.title: valve_cd indexes ld_table[0]/cd_table[0] without an empty-table guard; loader accepts empty cd_table
allConfirmed.description: valve_cd reads ld_table[0]/cd_table[0] (lines 168-169) and computes last = ld_table.len() - 1 (line 171). An empty table makes len() - 1 underflow to usize::MAX and the [0] index panic. The loader's unpack_cd_table (loader.rs:42-56) iterates the JSON array and produces empty Vecs for an empty `cd_table: []` array without rejecting it; those flow into cfg.intake_cd_table/exhaust_cd_table (loader.rs:168-169,178-179) -> ValveParams.cd_table (sdm26.rs:848-863) -> valve_cd with no intervening guard. valve_cd is reached once per open valve step (lift > 0), so any run with an empty cd_table crashes on the first valve-open step.
allConfirmed.impact: An engine config whose intake or exhaust cd_table is an empty JSON array passes loading and then panics the solver on the first valve-open step rather than being rejected up front. Severity low because the default config and all parity fixtures have non-empty tables; only an explicitly malformed config hits it.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Reject empty Cd/L-D tables in the loader (require arr non-empty in unpack_cd_table) and/or guard valve_cd to return 0.0 when ld_table.is_empty().
allConfirmed.verifier_note: valve.rs line 168 `if ld <= ld_table[0]` and line 171 `let last = ld_table.len() - 1;` are unguarded; loader.rs lines 46-54 push into ld/cd only inside `for row in arr` with no `arr.is_empty()` rejection, so an empty array yields empty tables that reach valve_cd via sdm26.rs:848-849/862-863.

allConfirmed.title: release_lock writes released_at using the client's wall clock (untrusted, skewable)
allConfirmed.description: build_release_lock_body() sets released_at = chrono::Utc::now() computed on the client and PATCHes it directly into the locks row instead of letting Postgres assign the timestamp. A client with a skewed or manipulated clock writes an inaccurate (even future/past) release time into an audit-relevant lock record, so lock-lifecycle ordering in history can become non-monotonic across clients. The code self-acknowledges this with a TODO at line 61.
allConfirmed.impact: Lock history / audit timestamps can be wrong or non-monotonic, undermining the 'who held the lock when' trail the PDM module relies on. Not a crash or data loss; a correctness/trust issue for an auditable system.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Assign released_at server-side via an RPC or DB trigger (released_at = now()) and stop sending a client-computed timestamp in the PATCH body.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: line 24 `json!({ "released_at": chrono::Utc::now() })` is client-computed and PATCHed at lines 63-72; the TODO at lines 60-62 explicitly notes 'the client clock is the source of truth for released_at'.

allConfirmed.title: extract_props_in can bind a property name to a <vt:> value belonging to a later property
allConfirmed.description: After reading a property name (search is set to the name's closing-quote offset, line 366), the value is taken from the FIRST '<vt:' found anywhere in `rest = &text[search..]` (line 381-382) with no bound limiting the search to the current <property>...</property> element. A value-less or self-closing <property name="X"/> that precedes a later <property name="Y"><vt:..>val</vt:..> causes X to be paired with Y's value. (Y is then also matched against the same <vt:> on the next loop iteration, so X ends up displaying Y's value.)
allConfirmed.impact: In unusual-but-valid property XML (mixed self-closed and valued <property> entries), a data-card field can display the wrong value. Best-effort parser, so impact is a misleading card row, not a crash; no security or data-loss consequence.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Bound the '<vt:' search to the current property element: find the next '</property>' or the next '<property name="' after the name and only search for '<vt:' before it; if none precedes that boundary, treat the property as value-less and skip it.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: line 366 `search = name_start + qrel` then line 381 `let rest = &text[search..]` and line 382 `rest.find("<vt:")` search the remaining text with no '</property>' boundary.

allConfirmed.title: No per-file cap on deflate-decode attempts on untrusted SolidWorks files (CPU/time DoS surface)
allConfirmed.description: scan_region() calls try_inflate(&bytes[i..]) at essentially every byte offset of the scanned region (i advances by consumed.max(1), but by only 1 whenever an offset does not begin a usable stream — line 124). Raw DEFLATE has no magic header, so any offset can begin a syntactically valid stream. The only bounds present are 64 MiB of output per individual attempt (line 290) and a 256 KiB inspect head; there is no cap on the NUMBER of inflate attempts per file, no wall-clock budget, and no cumulative-decompressed-bytes cap. For files <= 24 MiB the whole file is scanned (line 67-68), and a large file with no edge-window hit triggers a full middle scan (line 77-79). An adversarial file with many overlapping near-valid deflate framings can make a large fraction of up to ~24M offsets each spin up a DeflateDecoder that decompresses non-trivial output before rejection, giving roughly O(file_size) decode attempts.
allConfirmed.impact: A malicious .sldprt/.sldasm/.slddrw reaching a user via a shared vault or download can make parse_properties()/parse_refs() consume large CPU/time on preview or check-in. Runs on spawn_blocking so it won't freeze the UI thread, but can wedge a worker thread and stall check-in. Self-inflicted DoS only; no data loss or RCE.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Add a per-file (or per-region) cap on inflate attempts and/or a wall-clock budget, plus a cumulative-decompressed-bytes cap across attempts. A cheap pre-gate (plausible deflate block-header check, or only attempting at container record-framing offsets) would cut most wasted work.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Confirmed: scan_region loops `while i + 2 < end` advancing `i += 1` on every non-stream offset (lines 98,124); try_inflate's only ceiling is `if total_out > 64 * 1024 * 1024 { break }` (line 290) — no attempt-count or time budget anywhere.

allConfirmed.title: Non-comma (semicolon/tab) MoTeC and Link CSV exports fail to load
allConfirmed.description: For MoTeC/Link preamble files, strip_motec()/strip_link() rebuild the channel-name header via dedupe_csv_header(), which parses the original header with a default-COMMA csv::ReaderBuilder and re-serializes it with a default-COMMA csv::WriterBuilder. When the source export is semicolon- or tab-delimited (common in European-locale MoTeC and some Link configs), the comma reader sees no field separators and collapses the whole header into a SINGLE quoted cell (e.g. `"Time";"Engine Speed";"Throttle Position"` -> one cell `"Time;""Engine Speed"";""Throttle Position"""`). The data rows below are pushed verbatim. detect_delimiter() then runs on this rewritten header; because the embedded semicolons survive inside the quoted cell it actually selects ';' (not ',' as originally claimed), so the data rows split into N fields while the header is 1 field -> the csv reader returns Csv(UnequalLengths) and the whole file fails to load. (For a 2-column file or other layouts the failure can instead surface as the 'bad time' Malformed path, but the net effect is a hard load failure.)
allConfirmed.impact: A user importing a semicolon- or tab-delimited MoTeC/Link CSV (common in non-US locales) gets a hard load failure on a well-formed file. Plain (non-preamble) delimited CSVs are unaffected because detection runs on the raw first line and no header re-serialization occurs, so the failure is specific to vendor-preamble files.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Detect the delimiter from the ORIGINAL header/data line in strip_motec/strip_link before any re-serialization, and either re-serialize the deduped header with that same delimiter or carry the detected delimiter in CsvInput so load_csv_bytes reads with it directly instead of re-detecting from the rewritten text. dedupe_csv_header/count_csv_cells/parse_units_line must all use the source delimiter, not a hardcoded comma.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Empirically reproduced: a temp test through prepare_csv_input + load_csv_bytes gave LOAD(semicolon)=Err(Csv(UnequalLengths{expected_len:1,len:3})), LOAD_TAB=Err(Csv(UnequalLengths)), LOAD_COMMA=Ok(1). prepared.text header was the single mangled cell `"Time;""Engine Speed"";""Throttle Position"""` and detect_delimiter returned 59 (';'). Corrected the candidate's claimed mechanism (delimiter is not always ',' and error is UnequalLengths, not necessarily 'bad time') but the load-failure conclusion holds.

allConfirmed.title: compare alignment_key collision silently drops trials via BTreeMap overwrite
allConfirmed.description: Trials are inserted into a_by_key/b_by_key BTreeMaps keyed by alignment_key(t), which is built only from (rpm, overrides) and excludes trial_id. BTreeMap::insert silently overwrites on key collision, so any two trial rows sharing the same rpm + canonicalized overrides (e.g. two DOE sample rows that resolve to identical overrides at the same rpm, or externally-authored/schema-divergent NDJSON missing rpm where both fall back to rpm='?' overrides='{}') collapse into one entry — all but the last are dropped from both the aligned diff and the unmatched listing, with no warning.
allConfirmed.impact: compare can silently lose trials and produce a misleading diff with no indication. Blast radius is currently limited because run/sweep always emit a numeric rpm (verified: run.rs and sweep.rs both write "rpm": result.rpm) and the DOE sampler normally yields distinct override rows, but duplicate sample rows or hand-authored NDJSON trigger it.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Include trial_id (or row index) in the alignment key, or detect a key collision on insert (e.g. check contains_key before insert) and emit a warning / treat colliding rows as unmatched rather than overwriting.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: compare.rs:36 `a_by_key.insert(alignment_key(t), t.clone());` (and :40 for b) with key from alignment_key() which omits trial_id; insert overwrites silently. numeric_metric_keys explicitly skips 'trial_id' (line 167) confirming trial_id is not part of the alignment identity.

allConfirmed.title: MoTeC/Link units row and cell count parsed with hardcoded comma delimiter
allConfirmed.description: parse_units_line() and count_csv_cells() both build a csv::ReaderBuilder with the default COMMA delimiter. For a semicolon/tab-delimited MoTeC/Link export the units row is read as a single cell, so units beyond index 0 are blank and the semantic resolver (pass 2 in load_csv_bytes uses prepared.units.get(i) as unit_hint) loses the per-channel unit disambiguation hints. This shares the same hardcoded-comma root cause as the delimiter finding.
allConfirmed.impact: On non-comma vendor files, channel unit hints collapse to a single cell, degrading semantic mapping (e.g. kPa vs degC disambiguation). Largely subsumed by the delimiter finding because such files currently fail to load outright; this becomes the residual defect once the load-failure is fixed, so it should be fixed in the same pass.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Parse the units row and count cells using the same delimiter detected for the source file rather than hardcoding comma — naturally folded into the delimiter-propagation fix for finding 1.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Same temp test showed prepared.units = ["s;\"rpm\";\"%\""] — a single collapsed cell for a semicolon source. parse_units_line/count_csv_cells use `csv::ReaderBuilder::new()` with no .delimiter() call (lines 386, 399), i.e. default comma.

allConfirmed.title: cfd_load_capture interpolates unvalidated `job_id` into the read path, allowing directory traversal outside the captures root
allConfirmed.description: cfd_load_capture validates `file` against `..`/`/`/`\` (line 288) and whitelists it to pv.json/profiles.json/manifest.json (line 292), and whitelists `study_kind` (line 296), but `job_id` is joined directly into the read target at line 305 (`root.join(&job_id).join(&study_kind).join(rpm_int.to_string()).join(&file)`) with no traversal check and no canonicalize/contains guard. A `job_id` containing `..` segments escapes `<Documents>/Helios/cfd/captures` and lets the command read any JSON-parseable file matching the `/single-rpm|sweep/<u32>/{pv,profiles,manifest}.json` tail, returning its parsed content to the renderer. The asymmetry is confirmed by the sibling pure function `load_waves_from_dir` (crates/cfd-core/src/load.rs:56-58), which DOES reject `..`/`/`/`\` in `job_id` — and by `path_under()` (load.rs:16, already used at commands.rs:55) — proving the project knows to guard this field but missed it here.
allConfirmed.impact: A compromised/XSS'd renderer (same threat model the codebase documents for IPC commands) can read files outside the CFD captures directory whose path tail matches the expected layout, leaking their contents to the page. Constrained by the fixed `/<study_kind>/<rpm>/<whitelisted-file>` suffix, but a genuine directory escape the existing `file` validation was meant to prevent.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Reject `job_id` containing `..`, `/`, or `\` (or restrict to the ULID charset, since job ids are ULIDs) exactly as `load_waves_from_dir` already does, and after building `p` canonicalize it and verify `path_under(&p, &root)` before reading.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: commands.rs:305 `.join(&job_id)` has no preceding validation of job_id; contrast with crates/cfd-core/src/load.rs:56 `if job_id.contains("..") || job_id.contains('/') || job_id.contains('\\')` used by the sibling cfd_load_waves. Candidate's inclusion of cfd_load_waves in the bug is wrong — that path IS guarded.

allConfirmed.title: pdm.admin_delete_user lets a per-vault admin delete ANY non-admin user account globally (is_admin() has no vault filter)
allConfirmed.description: admin_delete_user is authorized solely by `if not pdm.is_admin()` (line 25). pdm.is_admin() (20260529000000_pdm_owner_role_and_admin_panel.sql lines 38-41) tests `role in ('owner','admin')` with NO vault_id filter, so a row with role='admin', vault_id=<some vault> (a PER-VAULT admin) satisfies it. The target-protection guards on lines 28-32 only look up the TARGET's global role to block deleting an owner or admin; they impose no scope check on the caller. Therefore a per-vault admin (a role the owner can legitimately grant via set_user_role, which only requires is_owner to mint an admin) can call pdm_admin_delete_user(any non-admin target) and permanently delete that user's auth.users row (line 59) plus null/reassign all their FKs across pdm/pm/support. The team explicitly recognized this exact `is_admin()`-admits-per-vault-admin flaw class as M6 and fixed it for audit_log in 20260619000400 by inlining a `vault_id IS NULL` predicate, but admin_delete_user was not given the same treatment.
allConfirmed.impact: A per-vault admin (scoped to a single vault by design) can permanently and irreversibly delete any non-admin user account in the entire org and reassign/null their authored data. Global-scope destructive operation that should require a global admin/owner.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Replace `if not pdm.is_admin()` with a global-only check (`exists(select 1 from pdm.user_roles where user_id = auth.uid() and role in ('owner','admin') and vault_id is null)`), mirroring the inline global-only predicate used for audit_log in 20260619000400, or introduce an is_global_admin() helper for all global operations.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Line 25 reads `if not pdm.is_admin() then raise exception 'not authorized'; end if;`. is_admin() body (20260529000000 L38-41) has no vault_id filter. rls-audit-log-scoping.test.ts L109-131 proves a `setVaultRole(perVaultAdmin.id,'admin',vaultId)` user satisfied the old is_admin() — confirming per-vault admins are creatable and pass this gate.

allConfirmed.title: pdm.admin_update_user lets a per-vault admin edit any non-admin user's profile globally (is_admin() not vault-scoped)
allConfirmed.description: admin_update_user is authorized solely by `if not pdm.is_admin()` (line 26), which (no vault_id filter) returns true for any per-vault admin row. The migration added owner/admin-tier TARGET guards (lines 33-40) but those only protect owner/admin targets and impose no scope check on the caller. A user who is admin in only one vault can therefore call the RPC against any non-admin user in the whole org and overwrite their display_name/subteam in auth.users metadata (lines 42-45). Same root cause the team deliberately avoided in the audit_log M6 fix (20260619000400 L33-47, which explicitly states it does NOT use is_admin() because it admits per-vault admins).
allConfirmed.impact: A per-vault admin can overwrite the display name / subteam of any non-admin user across the entire org, a global-scope mutation that should require a global admin. Reversible, hence medium.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Replace the `if not pdm.is_admin()` gate with a global-only admin check (`role in ('owner','admin') AND vault_id IS NULL`), consistent with the audit_log fix.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Line 26: `if not pdm.is_admin() then raise exception 'not authorized'; end if;`. The only other gates (L33,L38) test v_target_role of the TARGET, not the caller's scope.

allConfirmed.title: pdm.list_vault_roles and pdm.admin_list_users leak users' emails/roster to a per-vault admin (is_admin() not vault-scoped)
allConfirmed.description: list_vault_roles is gated by `if not (pdm.is_admin() or pdm.is_admin_in(p_vault_id))` (line 32). Because pdm.is_admin() ignores vault_id, a per-vault admin of vault X passes the is_admin() disjunct for ANY p_vault_id and can call pdm_list_vault_roles(other_vault) to enumerate every user's email, display_name, subteam and effective role for a vault they have no role in (the function returns auth.users.email + raw_user_meta_data, lines 36-49). The companion pdm.admin_list_users (20260531000000 L259-272) is gated by `pdm.is_admin()` alone and returns ALL users' emails org-wide, so a per-vault admin also gets the full org roster. This is the same cross-vault metadata-leak class the team closed for audit_log in 20260619000400, left open here.
allConfirmed.impact: A per-vault admin can read the full member roster (emails, names, roles) of vaults they have no role in, and the entire org-wide user list with emails via admin_list_users — cross-vault PII / metadata disclosure.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: For list_vault_roles, change the first disjunct to a global-only admin check so cross-vault listing requires a global admin while per-vault admins retain access via is_admin_in(p_vault_id). For admin_list_users, gate on a global-only admin check.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Line 32: `if not (pdm.is_admin() or pdm.is_admin_in(p_vault_id))`. is_admin() has no vault filter (20260529000000 L38-41), so the first disjunct admits any per-vault admin for any p_vault_id. admin_list_users (20260531000000 L263) is `if not pdm.is_admin()` and selects u.email for all auth.users.

allConfirmed.title: delete_folder force-releases other users' locks with no force_released_by attribution or force_unlock audit row
allConfirmed.description: pdm.delete_folder (SECURITY DEFINER) is the live, never-superseded definition (grep confirms delete_folder is only defined in this migration; later migrations only touch restore_folder). When a vault admin soft-deletes a folder whose subtree contains files checked out by OTHER users, it releases every active lock with a blanket `update pdm.locks set released_at = now() where released_at is null and file_id in (...)`. It does NOT set force_released_by on the displaced lock rows and writes NO force_unlock audit_log entry naming the displaced holders -- only a single 'delete'/'folder' audit row. delete_file (20260619000600) was explicitly given exactly this attribution (loops over locks held by user_id <> v_caller, stamps force_released_by, inserts a per-holder 'force_unlock'/'lock' audit row), but delete_folder -- which can displace many more holders at once -- was never given the same treatment. force_released_total in vault_insights_extra and per-lock force-unlock history rely on force_released_by being set, so this path silently under-reports forced unlocks.
allConfirmed.impact: An admin deleting a folder yanks active checkouts from other team members with zero attribution: displaced lock rows show released_at set but force_released_by NULL (indistinguishable from a voluntary check-in/cancel), and no force_unlock activity event is recorded. The activity history and the force_released_total insight under-count, and a displaced user has no audit trail showing who took their lock or why -- the exact gap the team already deemed worth fixing for the single-file delete path.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror the 20260619000600 delete_file pattern inside delete_folder: before the blanket release, loop over active subtree locks held by user_id <> v_caller, set released_at = now() and force_released_by = v_caller on each, and insert a 'force_unlock'/'lock' audit row per displaced holder (payload via='delete_folder', file_id, displaced_holder), each wrapped in begin/exception when others then null. Then release remaining caller-owned locks as today.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Lines 65-69 are a blanket `update pdm.locks set released_at = now() where released_at is null and file_id in (...)` with no force_released_by; contrast 20260619000600 delete_file lines 37-66 which loops `where ... and user_id <> v_caller`, sets `force_released_by = v_caller`, and inserts a 'force_unlock' audit row per displaced holder.

allConfirmed.title: reresolve_refs_for_file trigger re-resolves refs owned by soft-deleted parent assemblies (missing pf.deleted_at guard)
allConfirmed.description: pdm.reresolve_refs_for_file() (this migration is the latest definition; fires AFTER INSERT and AFTER UPDATE OF latest_version_id on pdm.files) re-resolves dangling child refs by unique basename. Its UPDATE joins pdm.versions pv -> pdm.files pf to reach the parent assembly but filters only `pf.vault_id = new.vault_id` and `r.child_file_id is null` -- it does NOT filter `pf.deleted_at is null`. The sibling deleted_at trigger handle_file_deleted_at_change (20260619000300, line 83) deliberately added `and pf.deleted_at is null` for exactly this case (labeled M-3: 'don't re-resolve refs owned by a soft-deleted PARENT assembly'), but that guard was never back-ported here. As a result, when a child file is created or first published, refs belonging to a soft-deleted (recycle-bin) parent assembly get their child_file_id/child_version_id re-populated, resurrecting Where-Used links for an assembly that is in the recycle bin.
allConfirmed.impact: Where-Used / reference data can show resolved child links hanging off assemblies that are soft-deleted, inconsistent with the deleted_at trigger's stated policy. Low impact because vault_insights_extra and the browse tree filter deleted parents, but direct refs reads for a restored child can momentarily show a deleted parent as a live consumer.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Add `and pf.deleted_at is null` to the UPDATE ... FROM pdm.versions pv join pdm.files pf predicate in reresolve_refs_for_file(), matching the M-3 guard already present in handle_file_deleted_at_change().
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Lines 97-102 join `pdm.files pf` with predicates `pf.vault_id = new.vault_id and r.child_file_id is null and lower(...)=lower(new.name)` -- no deleted_at filter. allConfirmed.title: add_and_lock resurrect path does not re-anchor soft-deleted ancestor folders (resurrected file orphaned from browse tree)
allConfirmed.description: When add_and_lock re-adds a name occupied by a soft-deleted tombstone, the resurrect branch (lines 65-81) clears deleted_at/deleted_by on the file row and re-acquires a lock, but does NOT re-anchor soft-deleted ANCESTOR folders the way restore_file does (20260619000200, BUG H4, lines 62-78: walk the folder_id parent_id chain clearing deleted_at on any soft-deleted ancestor folder, bounded against cycles). If a parent/ancestor folder of the resurrected file is still soft-deleted (e.g. an admin deleted the subtree, then an editor re-adds that file's name), the file becomes live but its folder_id still points at a deleted folder, so useFolders/the browse tree (which excludes deleted folders) hides it even though the RPC returned a valid file_id and lock_id. Secondary: the branch leaves published_at/created_by untouched, so resurrecting another user's never-published draft can return a file the caller cannot SELECT under files_read RLS until check-in publishes it -- a narrower edge case requiring a prior unpublished draft by a different user.
allConfirmed.impact: After recycle-bin churn: re-adding a file name whose ancestor folder is still soft-deleted resurrects a live file that does not appear in the tree (recoverable by restoring the folder). The created_by/published-draft visibility case is rarer. Low severity; uncommon delete/re-add sequence; recoverable.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: In the resurrect branch, after clearing deleted_at on the file, reuse the bounded ancestor re-anchor loop from restore_file (20260619000200) to clear deleted_at on soft-deleted ancestor folders. Optionally also stamp created_by = v_caller / publish on resurrect so the resurrecting user can always see the row.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Resurrect branch lines 66-75 only does `update pdm.files set deleted_at = null, deleted_by = null where id = v_deleted_file_id` plus re-lock -- no ancestor-folder walk. restore_file (20260619000200 lines 68-78) does the `while v_parent is not null loop ... update pdm.folders set deleted_at = null ... where id = v_parent and deleted_at is not null` re-anchor that this path lacks.

allConfirmed.title: import_version idempotency probe ignores soft-deleted files (chains versions onto tombstones)

If a file with that name was soft-deleted (recycle bin), re-importing it finds the tombstoned row and chains the new version onto it (lines 59-99), leaving the file's deleted_at set (invisible) rather than resurrecting it or treating it as a fresh import. add_and_lock was given explicit soft-delete awareness (20260618000300 -- LIVE probe + resurrect branch); import_version was never updated.

Service-role/system-only path, not user-exploitable, but a silent data-visibility bug on re-runs. Low severity.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Add tombstone handling to the idempotency probe: filter `deleted_at is null` and, on a matching deleted row, resurrect it (clear deleted_at/deleted_by) before appending the version, mirroring add_and_lock's resurrect path; or skip with a clear status so the importer is aware.
