allConfirmed.title: Hosted Task Pane control is never disposed on add-in disconnect — leaks a 4s polling timer that keeps hitting the bridge
allConfirmed.description: DisconnectFromSW() deletes the task pane view and sets _control = null (line 152) without ever calling _control.Dispose(). HeliosVaultControl is hosted in the task pane only by its HWND (DisplayWindowFromHandlex64, SwAddin.cs line 84), so SOLIDWORKS does not own its managed lifetime and DeleteView() does not dispose it. The control creates and Start()s a System.Windows.Forms.Timer (_pollTimer, Interval=4000) whose Tick handler calls RefreshConnection()/RefreshStatus(quiet:true) against the localhost bridge (HeliosVaultControl.cs lines 62-68). A running WinForms Timer's Tick delegate roots the control, so the GC.Collect()/WaitForPendingFinalizers() at the end of DisconnectFromSW (lines 158-159) cannot reclaim it. The control's own Dispose(bool) override (HeliosVaultControl.cs lines 72-80), which Stops/Disposes the timer and disposes the VaultTreePanel ImageList, is never invoked.
allConfirmed.impact: After the add-in disconnects (or is disabled/reloaded) without SOLIDWORKS exiting, the orphaned control + timer stay alive and keep firing an HTTP poll to 127.0.0.1 every 4 seconds for the life of the SOLIDWORKS process, plus a leaked WinForms control and the VaultTreePanel ImageList GDI handles. Repeated enable/disable cycles accumulate timers and handles. (On a full SOLIDWORKS shutdown the process exits anyway, which is why this is medium rather than high.)
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: In DisconnectFromSW, before `_control = null`, call `_control?.Dispose();` so the existing Dispose override stops/disposes _pollTimer and disposes VaultTreePanel's ImageList. Do this prior to GC.Collect.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: SwAddin.cs:152 `_control = null;` with no Dispose; HeliosVaultControl.cs:68 `_pollTimer.Start();` and :76-77 `_pollTimer?.Stop(); _pollTimer?.Dispose();` only in Dispose(bool), which is never called.

allConfirmed.title: Vault tree branch wedges permanently on 'Loading…' if the first /files call throws
allConfirmed.description: OnBeforeExpand sets _vaultLoading = true (line 218) then awaits LoadVaultModel() (line 219). LoadVaultModel always assigns _model = root (line 249) on the normal path, so a failed-but-returned bridge result is fine. However the await of _bridge.FilesAsync() (line 232) can throw: HeliosBridge.SendAsync guards ReadDiscovery and Http.SendAsync, but `await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()` (HeliosBridge.cs line 102) is NOT wrapped in try/catch and can fault on a mid-read connection drop. A thrown FilesAsync propagates into OnBeforeExpand's catch{} (line 227) AFTER _vaultLoading was set true and BEFORE _model is assigned. The guard at line 216 (`_model == null && !_vaultLoading`) is then false forever, so the Vault branch never retries on expand and stays on the 'Loading…' placeholder.
allConfirmed.impact: In a rare transient-error case the Vault tree is stuck on 'Loading…' until the user clicks the header Refresh, which calls InvalidateVault() (resets _vaultLoading=false, VaultTreePanel.cs line 161). Self-healing via Refresh, hence low severity.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Reset _vaultLoading = false in a finally block in OnBeforeExpand (or LoadVaultModel) so a thrown FilesAsync leaves the branch retryable on the next expand.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: VaultTreePanel.cs:218 sets `_vaultLoading = true;` with no finally; HeliosBridge.cs:102 `await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync()` is the one unguarded await that can throw out of FilesAsync.

allConfirmed.title: sw-helper read-only flip matches by exact normalized path string — divergent UNC/mapped/8.3 path forms silently no-op
allConfirmed.description: The helper normalizes via Norm() (forward→back slashes, trim trailing slash, ToLowerInvariant) and gates the flip on exact string equality `Norm(path) != target` (line 46). If SOLIDWORKS reports an open document's path in a textually different form than the desktop app passes (mapped drive Z:\ vs UNC \\server\share, or 8.3 short names), the loop skips it and returns exit 0 ('not open / nothing to do'), so the caller treats it as success. There is no canonical-path comparison or filename fallback.
allConfirmed.impact: On networked/mapped vault roots the in-session read-only flip after check-out/check-in can silently no-op, leaving the doc read-only in SOLIDWORKS after a successful check-out (or editable after check-in) until the user reloads. The on-disk read-only bit (set by the desktop app) is still the real guard — confirmed by the file header at Program.cs lines 19-21 — so this is a UX degradation, not data loss. Trigger depends on real-world path-form divergence, which is plausible but unproven here, hence low confidence.
allConfirmed.suggested_fix: Compare by canonical full path (GetFinalPathNameByHandle / file identity) instead of raw lowercased string equality, and/or fall back to a filename match when no exact path match is found.
allConfirmed.verifier_note: Program.cs:46 `if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(path) || Norm(path) != target) continue;` — exact normalized string compare only; Norm at :66-67 is just slash/trim/lowercase.

rejectedSamples.title: sweep-rpm-done matches the in-flight cycle buffer by exact RPM, mis-draining cycles on duplicate RPMs
rejectedSamples.reason: Premise is factually wrong. The candidate claims 'started/cycle/done events all carry rpmIdx' and proposes draining `inFlight[String(a.rpmIdx)]`, but the sweepRpmDone action does NOT carry rpmIdx (CfdContext.tsx:62 `{ type: 'sweepRpmDone'; id; point: Omit<SweepPoint,...>; captureDir? }`, and the dispatch at line 379 passes only point + captureDir). So `a.rpmIdx` is undefined and the suggested fix is invalid — rpm IS the only key the done event has. The candidate self-rates the impact 'cosmetic/diagnostic only … lastCycle stats on the point are still correct' and notes the normal path dedupes RPMs (parseRpmList); duplicate RPMs require a hand-built SweepParams bypassing dedup. Speculative edge case with a non-applicable fix; not a release-gate bug.

rejectedSamples.title: Provenance fields interpolated unescaped into lap-channel CSV comment header
rejectedSamples.reason: Not realistically exploitable and the formula vector is structurally defused. The three interpolated values are not free user text: configName = basename(study.configPath) (curveSources.ts:26) i.e. a filesystem basename which cannot contain CR/LF; vehicleName = runA.vehicle.name from preset/config tables; trackName = track.name from built-in constants (AUTOCROSS_2026/ENDURANCE_2026, LapSimScreen.tsx:118). None can carry a newline, so the CRLF comment-split claim has no source. The formula-injection claim also fails: every value is interpolated AFTER a literal prefix on its line (`# config: `, `# vehicle: `, `# event: … track: ` at lapChannelsCsv.ts:38-40), so a value can never be the first character of a cell where `=/+/-/@` would trigger. Author-rated low severity / low confidence, confined to comment lines, data rows already safe. Speculative style hardening, not a real bug.

rejectedSamples.title: paramForScatter / rankDim only initialised on mount can point at a parameter that does not exist after a study switch
rejectedSamples.reason: Real mechanism but it is the same root cause as the confirmed 'no remount key' finding — paramForScatter is seeded once (OptimizationResults.tsx:86-87) precisely because the component is not remounted on a same-kind study switch. Note also rankDim is not actually a 'nonexistent path' risk — it is reseeded from study.params.rankBy with a valid-metric guard (lines 91-93).

rejectedSamples.title: LapPlayer: animation loop continues to run after component unmount if `playing` and `endT` are both truthy at unmount time
rejectedSamples.reason: Not a real bug. Lines 540-552 show correct cleanup: `return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf)` properly cancels the outstanding RAF on unmount. In React 18, calling `setT` after unmount is a documented no-op (no warning, no corruption). The finding's own impact assessment says 'Benign in React 18 (no-op state update after unmount)' — this does not meet the bar for a confirmed bug. The suggested `unmounted` flag is a defensive style preference, not a correctness fix.

rejectedSamples.title: matchLocal reports 'synced' when both shas are undefined
rejectedSamples.reason: Not realizable. LocalFile.sha256 is typed non-optional `string` (useLocalFolderScan.ts line 8), and the scanner ALWAYS computes a sha (`sha = await sha256Hex(bytes)` line 117) before the only `out.push` that creates a LocalFile (line 121) — there is no code path that produces a LocalFile with an undefined sha256. Version.sha256 is also typed non-optional `string` (types.ts line 73). The bug requires BOTH `latest.sha256` AND `local.sha256` to be undefined simultaneously at line 66, but the local side is effectively never undefined, so `undefined === undefined` cannot occur in practice. Additionally line 61 already returns 'modified' when there is no version row, covering the most plausible missing-data case. This is speculation against a state the scanner and type system preclude.

rejectedSamples.title: BridgeOpHandler: listener registered once but closes over stale vaults/root on re-mount
rejectedSamples.reason: The code correctly handles both timing paths. If cleanup fires before the `.then()` resolves, `active` is set to `false` and the `.then()` callback hits the `else u()` branch (line 144), which calls the unlisten function immediately. The listener is never leaked. The stale-closure concern is also addressed by the refs at lines 75-84. No real bug exists.

rejectedSamples.title: BridgeOpHandler: `add` op uses `sizeBytes: 0`, bypassing size validation in useAddLocalFile
rejectedSamples.reason: Low-confidence speculation. The candidate itself concedes the server enforces limits independently. There is no evidence in the code that `useAddLocalFile` uses `sizeBytes` for any quota guard. This is a documentation issue at most, not a verifiable bug.

rejectedSamples.title: AdminScreen: role-select `onChange` fires `onSetRole` with the current value when the select is re-rendered while `pending`
rejectedSamples.reason: Speculative and browser-dependent. The `onChange` handler already guards with `if (v) onSetRole(u, v)` (only fires for non-empty values). The select is `disabled={busy}` during in-flight mutations (line 462), preventing interaction. The scenario requires a Firefox-specific spurious onChange that is not reliably reproducible and has no observed impact.

rejectedSamples.title: WhoHasWhatScreen: `submitForceUnlock` clears `reasonFor` before using `lockId`, then skips if reason empty — but `reasonFor` is already null
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate's own analysis concludes this is 'negligible in normal use' and 'the submit button is already disabled for empty reasons.' The silent no-op path described requires calling the function programmatically with an empty reason after the modal was already closed — not reachable through the UI. Not a real bug.

rejectedSamples.title: BulkActionBar: `eligibility` useMemo has `currentUserId` and `lockByFile` as deps but calls `lockKindFor` — missing dep causes stale closure
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate correctly self-corrects: `lockByFile` and `currentUserId` ARE in the dep array at line 127. When either changes, the memo re-runs and `lockKindFor` reads the current values. There is no stale closure.

rejectedSamples.title: BrowseScreen: Escape key listener on `window` does not use `stopImmediatePropagation` — clears tree selection when other modal Escape handlers run
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate concludes this is 'not a real bug' in its own analysis. The `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')` guard at line 412 prevents selection clearing whenever any dialog is open, correctly compensating for the sibling-listener issue.

rejectedSamples.title: FolderTree: `visibleItemsInOrder()` reconstructs the full visible order on every shift-click — O(N) allocation inside a click handler without memoization
rejectedSamples.reason: Performance observation only, not a correctness bug. The candidate rates confidence as medium and impact as potential lag on very large vaults. For a release gate this does not meet the bar of a genuine bug — it is a future optimization candidate.

rejectedSamples.title: PM cursor probe can miss a same-window delete+create (equal count, equal max(updated_at))
rejectedSamples.reason: Speculative and not supported by the code as the cited failure mode. The cursor (workspace-cursor.ts) explicitly tracks activity count (PmCursor.activity, fetched from the pm.activity feed), and a delete+create normally writes activity rows, so pmCursorChanged would detect it. The finding admits 'activity count would normally move' and only fails under a hypothetical 'any path that doesn't bump activity for both ops' that it does not demonstrate exists. The narrow remaining window is further covered by realtime (tasks is a published table) plus the focus and 180s backstop full refreshes, and the module doc-comment (lines 19-24) intentionally documents the long-tail tradeoff. Low-confidence speculation about an already-mitigated, self-acknowledged edge — not a release-gate bug.

rejectedSamples.title: expandEventsByDate guard of 800 iterations can still overflow for daily recurring events over multi-year windows
rejectedSamples.reason: The math does not support silent truncation. After the daily fast-forward (line 144-145), `cur` starts at `rangeStart`. The window passed to the function is always anchor±1yr = exactly 2 years ≈ 730 days, which fits within the 800-iteration cap. `seriesEnd` is also capped at `rangeEnd`, so the loop can run at most ~730 times for a daily event. The claim is speculative — the candidate acknowledges the window is 'just under the cap' but there is no confirmed code path that actually exhausts or exceeds 800.

rejectedSamples.title: BulkActionBar bulk-subteam move does not clear the subsystem from the in-memory TaskRow objects rendered in the current view
rejectedSamples.reason: Incorrect — the `embedTaskPatch` function (pmStore.ts lines 487-499 and 508-509) explicitly re-resolves both `.subteam` (when `subteam_id` is patched) and `.subsystem` (when `subsystem_id` is patched). `bulkUpdateTasks` calls `withSubteamMove` to add `subsystem_id: null` to the patch, then calls `embedTaskPatch` which sets `next.subteam = state.subteams.find(x => x.id === patch.subteam_id)`. Both the embedded subteam object and subsystem are updated atomically in the same store set.

rejectedSamples.title: TaskDetailSheet useEffect fires updateTask to clear subsystem_id whenever teamSubsystems changes, even during background refreshes
rejectedSamples.reason: The premise is incorrect. The store's `hydrate()` function (pmStore.ts lines 679-701) performs a single atomic `set()` that updates `subsystems`, `tasks`, and all other fields together in one React state update. There is no scenario where `subsystems` arrives in a separate render cycle from `tasks` during a background refresh. The effect's guard `if (!teamSubsystems.some(s => s.id === task.subsystem_id))` correctly returns early when the subsystem is still present, which it always will be after an atomic hydrate.

rejectedSamples.title: DayCreateMenu click-outside handler uses `mousedown` on `window`, which conflicts with dnd-kit pointer capture during active drags
rejectedSamples.reason: Speculative. The `mousedown` on `window` fires at the START of any drag, which means the menu closes immediately when dragging begins (correct behavior, not harmful). The re-open concern relies on dnd-kit synthesizing a click event after drag-end on the DayCell, but dnd-kit suppresses synthetic click events on elements that were part of a completed drag. No confirmed code path demonstrates the spurious re-open scenario.

rejectedSamples.title: GcalEventDetail dialog uses XSS-injectable text in `event.description` rendered via `whitespace-pre-wrap` — no sanitization
rejectedSamples.reason: Not a genuine security bug. React JSX escaping (`{event.description}`) prevents all HTML/script injection — this is React's fundamental XSS protection. The candidate acknowledges 'React JSX escaping prevents actual XSS.' The layout overflow concern from abnormally long strings is a minor UX issue, not a security or correctness bug. The `min-w-0 flex-1` container already provides some overflow containment.

rejectedSamples.title: Gantt SVG dependency arrows are drawn using all `deps` from the store, not just those between visible (filtered) bars
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate's own description explicitly states 'this is correct but undocumented' and 'this is the expected behavior.' A behavior the candidate itself labels as correct and expected cannot be classified as a bug. The null-return guard at line 860 (`if (!pred || !succ) return null`) cleanly handles the filtered-out case.

rejectedSamples.title: Snake game state not reset on remount if paused prop changes before restart
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate self-refutes the claim: it explicitly states 'No change needed — key remount already resets all refs' and 'acc.current = 0 after remount. Confirmed low impact.' Reading snake/index.tsx confirms acc is initialized as useRef(0) at line 18, so a key-bump remount re-executes the useRef(0) call and acc is always 0 on a fresh game. There is no stale accumulator scenario. The finding describes a non-bug.

rejectedSamples.title: Stale `workspaceId` closure in delete-workspace confirm handler may skip post-delete navigation
rejectedSamples.reason: The described failure mode does not hold up under scrutiny. The `onConfirm` closure at line 817-835 reads `workspaceId` from a React state snapshot, which is the expected and documented React closure behavior. The code comment at lines 818-820 shows the author explicitly addressed the stale-list race by using a functional updater for commitWorkspaces. For the `workspaceId` check at line 831: if the user switched away from the workspace being deleted before confirming, `workspaceId !== id` is true, so setWorkspaceId is correctly skipped — the user is already on a different workspace. If the user switched back to the deleted workspace after the dialog opened, the delete proceeds and nextActiveId is computed from the latest list via the functional updater. In no scenario does the code navigate to `workspaces[0]` as the finding claims. The net behavior is correct for all realistic race sequences, and the finding's impact description ("jumps to workspace[0]") is not supported by the code.

rejectedSamples.title: computeDistances integrates one sample past the lap end, over-counting lap distance at every boundary
rejectedSamples.reason: The asserted impact is incorrect. While the loop does read the sample at lap.endUs (`if (tUs > lap.endUs) break;` does not break on equality), the boundary-crossing trapezoid is NOT double-counted and the per-lap sum does NOT exceed the true total. Lap N+1 begins with prevT/prevV reset to NaN, so the first in-lap sample (the boundary sample) adds nothing to N+1 (`Number.isFinite(prevV)` is false on the first iteration); the boundary trapezoid is therefore attributed only to lap N. Attributing the boundary segment to the earlier lap is a defensible convention, not inflation. The finding's core claims ('each lap's distanceM is inflated by the final boundary trapezoid' and 'sum of per-lap distances exceeds the true total') are false, so this is rejected.

rejectedSamples.title: Lap cacheKey ignores manual crossing values (only hashes the count)
rejectedSamples.reason: Latent with no live impact. The finding itself concedes current callers do not dedupe on cacheKey. Verified via grep: LapSet.cacheKey is never compared for cache invalidation anywhere in production (only assigned synthetic strings in tests; the gps-track render.tsx cacheKey is an unrelated local variable). hashConfig's own contract explicitly tolerates collisions ('full equality isn't required... distinct configs collide rarely. Good enough for cache invalidation'). With no reachable consumer that would serve a stale LapSet, this is speculative hardening, not a release-gate bug.

rejectedSamples.title: percentile with out-of-range p produces NaN via undefined indexing instead of clamping
rejectedSamples.reason: Already handled at every call site; the trigger is unreachable. The only caller that passes a user-configurable p (friction-circle.tsx) guards with `if (!Number.isFinite(p) || p < 0 || p > 100) continue;` (line 53) BEFORE calling percentile. The other caller (bins.tsx) passes hardcoded literals 25/50/75. percentile documents 'p in [0, 100]' and that contract is honored at all call sites, so no out-of-range p ever reaches the indexing. This is a defensive-coding suggestion with no reachable production path.

rejectedSamples.title: FFT magnitudeSpectrum truncates the input to the nearest lower power of two, silently dropping up to ~half the samples
rejectedSamples.reason: Does not occur in practice; the documented caller contract is honored. The sole production caller (fft/render.tsx) computes `n = pow2Floor(iEnd - iStart)` itself (line 44) and passes exactly that many samples via `arr.subarray(iStart, iStart + n)` (line 52), so inside magnitudeSpectrum nIn === N and nothing is dropped. The widget also derives fs from the same truncated window and surfaces `n`, so the analyzed window length is reported, not hidden. The header comment 'callers pad or truncate to the nearest power of 2 before invoking' is accurate and followed. The truncation is a deliberate, visible widget-level decision, not a silent loss inside the helper.

rejectedSamples.title: computeLapDelta: early return from the middle of a block skips the refDist/refTimeS arrays built so far
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate correctly self-identified this as not a bug during its own analysis. Lines 70-75 form an if-block that early-returns when n !== refDist.length (NaN samples trimmed). Line 76 is only reached when n === refDist.length (no trimming needed). The logic is correct; the indentation is misleading but the behavior is sound.

rejectedSamples.title: GpsTrackRender: customTileUrl user input injected directly into MapLibre tile source without validation
rejectedSamples.reason: The 'SSRF' framing does not apply to a client-side desktop (Tauri) app — there is no server-side request. The tile URL is entered intentionally by the user in their own config. MapLibre's tile URL field accepts arbitrary https URLs by design. The Tauri IPC attack vector requires a specially crafted URL AND a misconfigured CSP; no evidence of either is present. This is speculative threat modeling, not a confirmed code-level bug in scope for a release gate.

rejectedSamples.title: XyPlotRender: draw() is an inner function called from effects and refs — captures stale visible from the render closure
rejectedSamples.reason: The candidate correctly self-downgraded to low confidence and found no real bug. The drawRef.current = draw pattern on every render keeps all closures fresh. The cursor subscription uses drawRef.current() indirection correctly. No stale closure path was identified.

rejectedSamples.title: ChannelPicker: unknown-channel sentinel option can be deselected, producing empty string silently submitted
rejectedSamples.reason: The component works as documented — allowEmpty is an explicit opt-in that intentionally allows '' as a value. Preventing channelId='' from being saved is the responsibility of the calling config editor, not the ChannelPicker component. This is a design contract issue, not a bug in the widget itself. No code path in ChannelPicker is incorrect.

rejectedSamples.title: SectorTableRender: sector comparison uses floating-point equality with 1e-6 epsilon but sectors may accumulate > 1e-6 error
rejectedSamples.reason: The bestS values in SectorTable are computed once in buildSectorTable (compute.ts line 58-66) from the same sectorS floats that appear in the rows. The render comparison at line 99 checks `Math.abs(v - table.bestS[k]) < 1e-6` where both v and table.bestS[k] are the exact same Float64 value stored in the same JavaScript arrays from a single computation pass. There is no second independent computation that could diverge. Math.abs(X - X) === 0, which is always < 1e-6. No precision loss path was demonstrated.

rejectedSamples.title: AtRpm objective uses a fixed +-0.5 RPM match window that can bind the wrong point for closely-spaced RPMs
rejectedSamples.reason: Code claim is literally accurate (objective.rs:81-88: target = rpm_int as f64; find with (r-target).abs() < 0.5 returns first match), but the impact is a contrived, unrealistic edge case for an engine RPM sweep. Triggering a wrong-point bind requires two RPMs less than 1.0 apart in the same objective rpm_list (e.g. 6000.0 and 6000.3). Engine RPM sweeps are integer-spaced and hundreds-to-thousands apart (codebase examples are 4000/6000/8000); nobody sweeps at sub-1-RPM granularity. The +-0.5 window correctly resolves every realistic input. The 'cannot address a fractional RPM' point is a minor API limitation, not a bug — rpm_int being u32 is the intended contract. This is a defensive-coding nicety / speculation about an input that does not occur in practice, not a genuine release-gate bug.

rejectedSamples.title: bmep_bar divides by rpm without the omega>0 guard used by adjacent torque calcs
rejectedSamples.reason: The unguarded `friction_power_w * 120.0 / rpm` at sdm26.rs:1267-1269 is genuinely unreachable, not just 'normally unreachable'. The division lives inside the cycle-boundary block gated by `if new_cycle > state.prev_cycle` (line 1246), where new_cycle = (state.theta / 720.0). theta only advances via `state.theta += dt * (180/PI) * omega` (line 1241), and omega = omega_from_rpm(rpm) = 2*PI*rpm/60 (kinematics.rs:8-10). So rpm==0 => omega==0 => theta never increments => new_cycle stays 0 => line 1267 is never entered. Reaching the division therefore requires a completed cycle, which requires theta to have advanced, which requires rpm > 0 — making the rpm denominator necessarily nonzero. No inf/NaN can be produced. This is a defensive-consistency nitpick about an impossible edge, not a real bug; the candidate itself concedes it is 'not reachable on the normal sweep path'. Reject.

rejectedSamples.title: MCP tools accept arbitrary read/write filesystem paths with no sandboxing
rejectedSamples.reason: Code claim is accurate (run_sim/submit_sweep write to an unvalidated out_path via ResultWriter::create -> File::create, validate_results reads an arbitrary ndjson_path, study/config paths likewise unconfined), but this is not a release-gate bug. The candidate self-rates it low and explicitly notes the standard MCP trust model treats the client/agent as trusted, and the entire impact is gated on a speculative 'if the server is ever exposed to less-trusted callers' hypothetical. Per the review bar this is an accepted trust assumption / latent hardening note, not a concrete defect — reject as speculation. (A doc note about the trust assumption is reasonable but it is not a confirmed bug.)

rejectedSamples.title: cfd_load_waves leaves `job_id` and `study_kind` unvalidated at the command edge
rejectedSamples.reason: Refuted. cfd_load_waves (commands.rs:325-336) delegates to cfd_core::load::load_waves_from_dir, which validates `job_id` against `..`/`/`/`\` (load.rs:56-58) and whitelists `study_kind` (load.rs:59-62) before joining the path. There is even a dedicated regression test `rejects_path_traversal_in_job_id` (load.rs:249-255) and `rejects_invalid_study_kind` (load.rs:257-263). The traversal claim is valid ONLY for cfd_load_capture, which is confirmed separately; the cfd_load_waves half of the candidate is incorrect.

rejectedSamples.title: Autostart preference marker falls back to temp dir when LOCALAPPDATA is unset, allowing first-run default to clobber a user's opt-out
rejectedSamples.reason: Speculative / not realistically reachable. The fallback to std::env::temp_dir() (lib.rs:30) only triggers when LOCALAPPDATA is unset, but LOCALAPPDATA is a standard Windows user environment variable present in essentially every interactive user session — the only consumer of this Windows-targeted autostart path. The harm further requires the temp dir to be cleared between sessions AND that to coincide with the rare missing-LOCALAPPDATA state. This is a chain of exotic preconditions outside the documented threat model rather than a reachable defect. The swallowed write error in mark_autostart_preference_set (lib.rs:42) is intentional best-effort behavior with negligible impact (worst case the default re-applies once). Rejecting as low-confidence speculation.

rejectedSamples.title: Auto-provision trigger grants every new signup global 'editor' write access with no domain/allowlist restriction
rejectedSamples.reason: REJECTED as speculative + intentional-design. The risk is entirely conditional on a Supabase project-level setting (whether public signups are enabled) that does not exist in the code under review and cannot be verified from these migration files — the finding itself concedes it is 'moot' if signups are invite-only/disabled and self-rates low confidence. The migration header (20260619000700 lines 9-18) explicitly documents the global 'editor' default as an intentional single-team design decision, deliberately withholding admin/owner and explaining why editor (not viewer) is chosen. The code does exactly what it states; there is no defect in the SQL. This is a configuration/policy recommendation, not a code bug, and does not meet the bar for a confirmed release-gate finding.

rejectedSamples.title: Add-in registration writes the discovery list entry to HKCU, but SOLIDWORKS only reads HKLM — add-in never loads
rejectedSamples.reason: Does not match the current code. The Rust injector (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/addin_injector/registry.rs) writes the discovery list entry to HKLM, not HKCU: register_hklm_list_elevated() (lines 81-101) imports `[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\SolidWorks\AddIns\{GUID}]` via an elevated reg import, and hklm_list_entry_present() (lines 71-75) verifies it under HKLM. register_per_user() (lines 31-58) writes ONLY the per-user CLSID and the AddInsStartup enable flag to HKCU — it never writes the AddIns list entry to HKCU. SwAddin.cs lines 42-61 likewise write the list entry to HKLM and the enable flag to HKCU, which is correct. This is the previously-fixed HKLM-registration bug; the candidate's premise (entry written to HKCU) is no longer true. The 'verified on this machine HKLM does not exist' note is runtime state, not a code defect — the code path that writes HKLM exists and is gated behind the elevated provisioning step the module documents.

rejectedSamples.title: Active-document type check uses doc.GetType() which may bind to System.Object.GetType()
rejectedSamples.reason: Speculation / style, not a present bug. The candidate's own reasoning shows it cannot currently be wrong: `doc.GetType() != (int)swDocumentTypes_e.swDocASSEMBLY` (SwAddin.cs:180) compiles and ships, which is only possible if GetType() binds to the SolidWorks IModelDoc2 interop method returning int (Object.GetType() returns System.Type and `Type != int` would not compile). The concern is a hypothetical future refactor changing binding, not actual behavior. The redundant guard is also harmless: the real assembly detection is the `doc is IAssemblyDoc asm` cast on the next line (182). No correctness defect in the code as written.
